El debate de candidatos catalanes a las elecciones generales del 29-N, en directo | PP y Vox abogan por limitar la inmigración mientras Urtasun defiende la regularización de migrantes
items.description: Tras la huelga general de este miércoles y a pocas horas del arranque oficial de la campaña electoral, EL PAÍS y la Cadena SER celebran este jueves un debate con los principales candidatos catalanes al 29-N: Jordi Hereu (PSC), Ernest Urtasun (Frente Amplio), Jordi Albert (ERC), Míriam Nogueras (Junts), Xavier García Albiol (PP) y Carina Mejías (Vox). en el bloque de inmigración, PP y Vox han defendido “limitar” la inmigración, con Mejías afirmando que “los que han venido a vivir de las ayudas, a delinquir o a violar, fuera”. Urtasun se ha mostrado orgulloso de la regularización de migrantes, mientras que Hereu le ha reprochado a albiol su racismo. Nogueras ha reclamado más control y ha reclamado las competencias en la materia para Cataluña. Albert ha rechazado relacionar inmigración y delincuencia. En vivienda, Junts ha defendido su rechazo al decreto que hoy se vota en el Congreso porque “no soluciona el problema”, lo que ha ocasionado un choque con Urtasun, que ha defendido con Hereu que este jueves sean aprobados en la Diputación Permanente. Por su parte, Albiol ha denunciado que el decreto “pone al mismo nivel a las familias vulnerables y a los jetas”. Después, las infraestructuras, especialmente Rodalies, han tomado el protagonismo. Albiol ha achacado los problemas a la falta de presupuestos del Gobierno y Mejías, a la corrupción en el Ministerio de Transportes. Nogueras ha reclamado el traspaso integral y Urtasun, más inversión. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Última hora de la actualidad política, en directo | Rufián, sobre las actuaciones policiales en las manifestaciones por la vivienda: “No hay que descargar de responsabilidad al PSOE”
items.description: El cabeza de lista de ERC al Congreso, Gabriel Rufián, ha pedido este jueves que “no se descargue de responsabilidad al PSOE” por las actuaciones policiales ocurridas ayer miércoles en Madrid y en otros lugares durante las manifestaciones por la vivienda. “No hay que descargar de responsabilidad al PSOE, que al final siempre se va de rositas. El PSOE gobierna el país y, si la policía le da de hostias a la gente en la calle por la cara, alguna responsabilidad tendrá”, ha dicho. El ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande Marlaska, ha ordenado al director general de la Policía que se investiguen específicamente estas actuaciones policiales. Además, ha dado la orden de que, en lo sucesivo, no se use gas lacrimógeno en los dispositivos de control de manifestaciones. Tanto el cabeza de lista de Frente Amplio por Madrid, Emilio Delgado, como la portavoz de Podemos en el Congreso, Ione Belarra, han pedido la destitución de Marlaska. El ministro de Presidencia, Félix Bolaños, considera que la huelga ha tenido “efectos muy positivos” porque se han llevado al debate público los temas que “importan” a los ciudadanos, mientras que la portavoz del PP, Ester Muñoz, y Vox han asegurado que fue “un fracaso”. Por otro lado, la Diputación Permanente del Congreso convalidará este jueves, salvo sorpresa, uno de los dos decretos ley de vivienda que aprobó el Gobierno el pasado 6 de octubre a raíz del desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal , de 87 años. items.title: Withheld ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌​‍‍⁠​​‌​LG funds: Osun workers resume after three-day warning strike
items.description: Government workers in Osun resumed duty on Thursday after putting off their three-day warning strike called by the organiser labour for the release of funds due to local governments in the state by the Federal Government. The News of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the gates of the state government secretariat in Abere and Osun Assembly, shut since Monday, were reopened with workers back to work. Similarly, workers in Olorunda and Osogbo Local Government Secretariats were also back to their duty posts. NAN reports that organised labour in the state had on Sunday directed workers to embarked on solidarity strike with local government workers for the release of the withheld council allocations. The organised labour comprising the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Trade Union Congress (TUC) and Joint Negotiating Council (JNC), however, on Wednesday directed workers to resume duty today. The organised labour appreciated workers, pensioners and affiliate unions for their support, cooperation and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “The organised labour expresses its profound appreciation to all affiliate unions, workers, pensioners and members for their unwavering solidarity, cooperation and exemplary conduct throughout the three-day sympathy strike in support of the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE), Osun Council. “We commend all members for their commitment, discipline, unity and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “Your solidarity has once again demonstrated the strength of the labour movement and our collective resolve to defend workers’ rights, welfare and dignity. “Accordingly, all workers are hereby directed to resume work at midnight Nov. 11. “All affiliate unions and their members are enjoined to comply fully with this directive and return to their respective workplaces,” it said. The organised labour urged workers to remain calm, united and steadfast, while maintaining mobilisation and remaining on standby for further directives. (NAN) The post Withheld ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌​‍‍⁠​​‌​LG funds: Osun workers resume after three-day warning strike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: At COP31, PM Shehbaz calls for grant-based finance, resilience funding for climate-vulnerable countries
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday called for grant-based finance and improved resilience and adaptation funds for climate-vulnerable countries at COP31, being held in Turkiye’s Antalya. This year’s summit focuses on transitioning toward a low-carbon future. Delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya as global greenhouse gas emissions show little sign of falling, while wars, inflation and other crises compete for political attention. Addressing the summit, PM Shehbaz highlighted Pakistan’s efforts to promote clean energy but warned that “national effort cannot replace a fair and just global response”. “When climate disasters strike, vulnerable countries need timely help and finance that does not deepen their debt,” he said, adding that Pakistan called for “grant-based finance, including public-private partnerships, alongside a significant increase in resilience and adaptation funds, which amount to survival funds, especially for struggling economies”. He said clean energy sources accounted for nearly 55pc of Pakistan’s energy needs, adding that the country was advancing electric mobility and had set a target of reducing projected emissions by about 50pc by 2035. Recalling the 2025 floods in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Buner district, the prime minister said: “In August 2025, a young man in Buner was just two days away from his wedding when flash floods swept through his village. A home preparing for celebrations became a house of mourning.” “Their grief was personal, yet the warning signs were global,” the prime minister said, noting that this was the story of “millions of people in Pakistan and across the developing world”. “People who have contributed the least to climate change bear its heaviest consequences,” he added. Addressing the summit, PM Shehbaz also recalled the 2022 floods in Pakistan, noting the economic damage and mass displacement the catastrophe caused. More than 1,700 people lost their lives, and economic losses exceeded $30bn,” the prime minister said. PM Shehbaz recalled his speech at the UN General Assembly in 2022. “I had warned that what is happening in Pakistan will not stay in Pakistan, and unfortunately, that warning has become a stark reality. “The future we feared has become the present we are living,” he said. Underscoring the need for global solidarity, the premier remarked, “Climate change knows no borders and no nation can face it alone. Solidarity must mean real action.” He then expressed gratitude to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan for his country’s support for Pakistan during the 2010 and 2022 floods. Addressing the summit, PM Shehbaz also warned against the weaponisation of water. “No nation should be allowed to put the lives and livelihoods of people downstream at risk. Water-sharing agreements must be honoured in letter and spirit,” the premier said. Concluding his address, PM Shehbaz said world leaders had gathered at the summit to “shoulder a shared responsibility to protect life on this earth.” “Let our success be measured not by promises we make here but by the families we protect, the resources we deliver, and the meaningful action we sustain,” he hoped. Meetings on the sidelines of the summit Separately, PM Shehbaz met President of Sudan’s Transitional Sovereignty Council General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya. According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s longstanding ties with Sudan and reiterated Islamabad’s support for the country’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity. He also expressed solidarity with the Sudanese people amid the prevailing challenges. The two leaders had a productive exchange on ways to further strengthen bilateral relations in various areas of mutual interest, it added. They also exchanged views on the challenges posed by climate change and emphasised the importance of enhanced international cooperation to address its impact, particularly on developing countries. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining close coordination at multilateral forums, it said. The premier also held a meeting with the president of Finland, Alexander Stubb. According to the PMO, the meeting “provided an opportunity to review Pakistan–Finland relations and strengthening cooperation in areas of mutual interest”. It said PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s desire to “translate the longstanding and friendly relations into a forward-looking partnership encompassing trade and investment, education and skills development, technology, climate resilience and people-to-people contacts”. He also noted the considerable potential to increase bilateral trade and welcomed the presence of Finnish companies in Pakistan, it added. The statement said PM Shehbaz also encouraged greater business-to-business engagement, technology transfer and investment in telecommunications, advanced manufacturing, clean technologies and mining. “The two leaders exchanged views on climate change, disaster risk reduction and environmental cooperation. The prime minister expressed interest in Finnish technical expertise in flood forecasting, water management, climate-resilient agriculture, glacier monitoring and early-warning systems,” the statement said. “Underlining the importance of dialogue, mediation and peaceful settlement, the two leaders exchanged views on ongoing diplomatic efforts for peaceful and durable solutions to the conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia,” it added. The statement further said that President Stubb appreciated Pakistan’s role in facilitating dialogue and mediation between the US and Iran. “The two leaders reaffirmed the importance of maintaining regular engagement and exploring practical avenues to deepen bilateral cooperation. The prime minister reiterated the invitation to President Stubb to undertake an official visit to Pakistan at a mutually convenient time,” it said. Further, the prime minister also met the president of Iraq, Nizar Mohammed Saeed Amidi. The PMO said PM Shehbaz congratulated President Amidi and the people of Iraq on the successful conduct of parliamentary elections and formation of the new government. “He reaffirmed Pakistan’s steadfast support for Iraq’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, national unity and stability,” it said. “The two leaders reaffirmed the longstanding brotherly relations between Pakistan and Iraq, rooted in shared faith, historical bonds and strong people-to-people contacts. Expressing satisfaction over the positive momentum in bilateral relations, they underscored the importance of sustained high-level exchanges and institutional engagement,” the statement said. The statement said that the premier also extended an invitation to President Amidi to visit Pakistan at a mutually convenient time. “The two sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral cooperation, with particular focus on trade, investment, manpower, reconstruction, agriculture, and defence,” the statement said. “The prime minister appreciated Iraq’s facilitation for Pakistani zaireen (pilgrims). The two leaders also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment for close coordination at multilateral fora,” it said. Pakistan stresses clean energy On Tuesday, PM Shehbaz addressed a high-level dialogue on clean energy transition, titled ‘ 35 by 35: Powering the Future ’, where he highlighted Pakistan’s solar power boom. “In just two years, Pakistan has added nearly 22 gigawatts of rooftop solar capacity — a quiet revolution by ordinary citizens seeking affordable power and a cleaner, more predictable future.” He had affirmed that Pakistan fully supports the ‘ 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge ’, wherein countries agree to aim to increase electricity’s share of total final energy consumption to around 35 per cent by 2035 in line with global climate objectives. The prime minister also held several bilateral conversations with world leaders and international organisations on the sidelines of the summit on Wednesday. Dozens of leaders are speaking during the “ high-level segment ” taking place on Wednesday and Thursday, including Erdogan, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year’s climate talks. “Nature — no less than people — is also paying a heavy price for armed conflicts. The starkest example of this is Gaza… what has taken place in Gaza is not only a genocide, but it is also an ecocide,” Erdogan said to applause on Wednesday. The United States, the world’s largest historical emitter, has skipped the talks for the second year in a row after President Donald Trump — who has called global warming a hoax — withdrew the US from climate cooperation following his return to office in 2025. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement on a plan to increase the share of electricity in global energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels. On Wednesday, the UN chief told world leaders at the summit that the slow international response to climate change so far had placed the world on a path to destruction. Governments must fight harder to preserve the planet for future generations, he said, in comments that set the tone for two days of rapid-fire speeches by world leaders. “The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us. This is the path to mutually assured destruction,” Guterres said, pointing to rising emissions, global temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters. “But science is not telling us to surrender. It is telling us to fight harder.”

items.title: El telescopio espacial ‘Euclid’ detecta 900 millones de galaxias y comienza el mapa tridimensional del universo
items.description: Una misión europea despegó hace tres años con el encargo de responder algunas de las preguntas más trascendentales de la humanidad: ¿De qué está hecho el universo? ¿Dónde está el planeta Tierra exactamente? ¿De dónde venimos? El cohete, con el telescopio espacial Euclid a bordo, despegó el 1 de julio de 2023. Este jueves se publican sus primeros resultados sustanciales. El aparato ha analizado una superficie del cielo equivalente a 9.500 lunas llenas y ha detectado 900 millones de galaxias, las piezas necesarias para que los científicos empiecen a ensamblar el primer puzle tridimensional detallado del universo. items.title: Burkina Faso : 37 136 personnes rapatriées après les événements en Guinée, selon le CONASUR
items.description: Le Burkina Faso a enregistré au 11 novembre 2026, un total de 37 136 personnes rapatriées à la suite des événements survenus en Guinée. C'est ce qui ressort du communiqué du Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR), publié par le ministère de la Famille et de la solidarité. Il est souligné que 10 512 personnes supplémentaires ont été accueillies et enregistrées au cours de cette journée, avec l'arrivée du quatrième convoi. Sur les 37 136 personnes rapatriées, le bilan fait état de 36 191 hommes et de 945 femmes. Parmi elles figurent également 7 988 enfants et 1 049 ressortissants d'autres nationalités. Le CONASUR précise que cette nouvelle arrivée a été rendue possible grâce à la mobilisation de plusieurs moyens de transport, notamment des cars mis à disposition par la partie malienne, ainsi qu'à des initiatives individuelles. Le Conseil salue l'appui de l'ensemble des parties prenantes ayant contribué au bon déroulement des opérations. Le ministère de la Famille et de la solidarité, à travers le CONASUR, réaffirme son engagement à poursuivre les efforts pour assurer le retour, l'accueil et la prise en charge des compatriotes dans des conditions sécurisées et respectueuses de leur dignité. Le Conseil invite par ailleurs les populations à maintenir leur élan de solidarité envers les personnes rapatriées. Il les appelle également à faire preuve de responsabilité dans le partage des informations, en privilégiant les sources et les canaux officiels. Lire le communiqué ci-dessous. items.title: Éducation : après dix ans de réformes, une transformation encore inachevée

items.title: Imperial General Assurance provides GH₵150m insurance cover for Mfantsipim @150 celebrations
items.description: Imperial General Assurance has announced a comprehensive insurance package valued at GHS150 million to support activities marking the 150th Anniversary celebrations of Mfantsipim School, one of Ghana’s most prestigious secondary educational institutions. The insurance cover will provide protection against accidental injuries and related liabilities arising from all activities and events organised as part of the Mfantsipim @150 celebrations, including the highly anticipated Grand Durbar, which is expected to attract thousands of alumni, students, dignitaries and guests from across Ghana and beyond. The support reinforces Imperial General Assurance’s commitment to safeguarding major national events and providing peace of mind for organisers and participants throughout the celebrations. The Managing Director of Imperial General Assurance, Harry Ofori-Attah, said the partnership reflects the company’s commitment to supporting institutions that have made significant contributions to Ghana’s development. “Mfantsipim School has, for 150 years, been a beacon of excellence, discipline and leadership in Ghana. We are proud to support this historic milestone with a GHS150 million insurance cover that provides peace of mind to organisers, participants and guests throughout the anniversary celebrations.”, he said. He noted that beyond celebrating the school’s rich heritage, it was important to ensure that all activities associated with the anniversary were backed by robust risk protection. “This partnership reflects our commitment to protecting institutions that have made significant contributions to national development. As thousands gather for the Mfantsipim @150 activities, including the Grand Durbar, we are pleased to provide comprehensive protection against accidental injuries and related liabilities, ensuring a safe and memorable celebration for all.” The Mfantsipim @150 celebrations are expected to feature a series of commemorative activities leading up to the Grand Durbar, bringing together generations of alumni, students, faculty and distinguished guests to celebrate the school’s enduring legacy and impact on education and leadership development in Ghana. Imperial General Assurance is Ghana’s fastest-growing insurer and is a member of Ghana Club 100 and the African Insurance Organisation (AIO).

items.title: Imran’s sisters Uzma, Noreen released from jail after extended detention orders withdrawn, says lawyer
items.description: LAHORE: Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, sisters of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, were released from Kot Lakhpat jail following the withdrawal of their extended detention orders, PTI legal counsel Rana Mudassar Umer told Dawn on Thursday. In a post on X, he said the two — who were detained in September under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance (MPO) along with their sister Aleema Khan — had returned home “safely”. PTI lawyer Taimur Malik also said on X that the two women had been released upon the withdrawal of the “unlawful MPO detention order”. “Everyone else detained under these MPO orders should be released as well,” he said. Imran’s three sisters — Noreen, Aleema and Uzma — have been in jail on the Lahore deputy commissioner’s (DC) orders as the PTI geared up for a protest march towards Islamabad. Their detention was initially ordered for 30 days. Their detention was then challenged in the Lahore High Court after the 30-day period lapsed last month, following which the Punjab government informed the court that it had been extended for another 30 days. Aleema, who was the first to be detained, still remains in jail. On Oct 28, Noreen was moved from Kot Lakhpat jail to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) due to high blood pressure. At the time, her lawyer claimed that no family member had been informed about her deteriorating health. The PTI had also condemned Noreen’s transfer to the PIC without informing her family, expressing grave concern over her health and the treatment of “political prisoners”. However, the government had insisted that she was “fine” after being provided medical treatment. “As per the information available, she is fine and all her medical tests are normal,” the adviser to the prime minister on political affairs, Rana Sanaullah, had informed the Senate on Oct 29.

items.title: Coopération militaire : Bamako et l’AFRICOM examinent les possibilités d’un appui américain
items.description: © Internet Assimi Goïta a reçu mardi le général Dagvin Anderson à Koulouba. L’entretien a porté sur la menace armée au Sahel et les perspectives de coopération avec les États-Unis. La rencontre s’est tenue pendant le séjour au Mali du commandant de l’United States Africa Command, venu dans le cadre du Salon international de la défense et de la sécurité de Bamako. Le ministre délégué auprès du ministre de la Défense et des Anciens combattants, le général de division Oumar Diarra, assistait à l’audience. Le compte rendu publié après l’entretien indique que les échanges ont concerné la situation sécuritaire au Mali et dans les pays voisins. Les deux responsables ont aussi abordé les formes possibles d’un soutien américain à la lutte contre les groupes armés. Dagvin Anderson a déclaré que son équipe souhaitait examiner avec Bamako les moyens susceptibles d’être réunis. Il a affirmé avoir mieux compris la perception malienne de la menace et évoqué une volonté de travailler avec le Mali ainsi qu’avec les autres États du Sahel. Ces propos expriment une intention de coopération. Ils ne correspondent pas encore à l’annonce d’un programme militaire, d’une assistance financière ou d’une livraison d’équipements. Modalités Les domaines précis, le calendrier et les moyens restent à définir. Le compte rendu de l’audience ne mentionne pas la signature d’une convention ni le lancement d’un programme de formation, d’équipement ou de partage de renseignements. Le général américain a également affirmé qu’Assimi Goïta était le premier chef d’État sahélien rencontré par son équipe dans le cadre de cette démarche. Cette indication place Bamako au début d’une consultation régionale annoncée par l’AFRICOM. Les prochaines étapes et les autres pays concernés n’ont pas été précisés. La présence de Dagvin Anderson au Salon international de la défense a facilité l’entretien politique. BAMEX réunit des responsables militaires, des industriels et des délégations étrangères autour des équipements, de la formation et de la coopération technique. La participation au salon ne vaut toutefois ni commande ni accord de défense. Autre audience Après le commandant de l’AFRICOM, le président de la Transition a reçu Abass Mohamadi, vice-ministre iranien de la Défense chargé des affaires industrielles et de la recherche. Cette seconde rencontre s’est également déroulée en présence du général Oumar Diarra. Le compte rendu public fournit peu de détails sur les sujets abordés avec le responsable iranien. La présence, le même jour, de délégations américaine et iranienne à Koulouba reflète surtout la diversité des participants reçus pendant BAMEX. Chaque audience relève d’une relation bilatérale distincte. La rencontre avec l’AFRICOM ouvre une discussion entre Bamako et Washington. Sa portée se précisera avec la publication éventuelle d’accords, de programmes ou de moyens affectés à cette coopération.

items.title: Dundal JOJ : le Centre culturel régional de Louga promeut les jeux traditionnels
items.description: Depuis vendredi dernier, le Centre culturel régional Mademba Diop de Louga organise des activités autour des jeux traditionnels et des veillées culturelles dans le cadre de « Dundal », en prélude aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. « À Louga, nous avons proposé un programme de promotion et de valorisation des jeux traditionnels », a indiqué la directrice du Centre culturel régional Mademba Diop de Louga, Ndèye Gnagna Diallo. À cet effet, elle a précisé qu’un village dédié aux jeux traditionnels a été aménagé. Parmi les activités proposées figurent notamment la course aux œufs, le jeu de penalty et la danse. Selon Ndèye Gnagna Diallo, cette initiative vise à faire redécouvrir aux adolescents et aux jeunes leur patrimoine culturel. « Nos parents pratiquaient ces jeux pour inculquer aux enfants des leçons de morale et de vie », a-t-elle expliqué. D’autres activités se sont également déroulées dans différentes localités de la région. Ainsi, une veillée culturelle a été organisée dans la commune de Sagatta Gueth, dans le département de Kébémer. « Comme ici, il y a eu des jeux traditionnels, suivis d’une animation culturelle », a fait savoir la directrice. Dans la même dynamique, des séances de « kassack », un chant initiatique et traditionnel, ont été organisées à Dahra Djoloff, dans le département de Linguère. Ces différentes activités ont enregistré une forte mobilisation, notamment des enfants et des élèves. À ce titre, Mme Diallo a vivement remercié l’Inspection d’académie de Louga ainsi que les différents établissements scolaires qui ont répondu favorablement à l’invitation. Falel Pam

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : derrière les lumières de la ville, un savoir-faire sénégalais !
items.description: À la veille de la clôture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (Joj) Dakar 2026, prévue ce vendredi, le Sénégal aura démontré au monde sa capacité à accueillir et à organiser un événement sportif international de grande envergure. Des infrastructures sportives aux cérémonies, en passant par les chorégraphies et l'habillage de la capitale, cette réussite repose également sur une mobilisation de compétences nationales. Dans les coulisses de cette transformation urbaine, des entreprises sénégalaises ont apporté leur expertise. Les Joj Dakar 2026 auront été bien plus qu’une compétition sportive. Pour le Sénégal, cet événement constitue une vitrine de ses capacités organisationnelles, techniques et humaines. Pendant plusieurs jours, Dakar et les autres sites de compétition ont accueilli des milliers d'athlètes, de délégations et de visiteurs venus des quatre coins du monde. Une mobilisation qui a nécessité, au-delà des équipements sportifs, un important travail d'aménagement et de mise en valeur des espaces urbains. Lire aussi: JOJ Dakar 2026 : le savoir-faire sénégalais derrière la magie du spectacle Car, derrière les images des cérémonies, les installations sportives et les décors lumineux qui ont accompagné cette fête du sport, il y a aussi des femmes et des hommes, des techniciens, des ingénieurs et des ouvriers sénégalais. Leur savoir-faire a contribué à donner à la capitale un visage à la hauteur de cet événement international. Parmi les entreprises mobilisées figure Ert (Études réalisations techniques), qui a accompagné la Ville de Dakar dans plusieurs chantiers liés aux préparatifs des Joj. Ses interventions ont notamment porté sur la réhabilitation de réseaux d'éclairage public, l'installation de dispositifs de branding lumineux et la mise en place de feux de signalisation tricolores. Sur le volet de l’éclairage public, les travaux ont concerné plusieurs axes stratégiques de la capitale, notamment la Corniche Ouest, du rond-point des Mamelles au Bloc des Madeleines, l'avenue Blaise Diagne, l'avenue Bourguiba et les Allées Seydou Nourou Tall. Ces interventions ont permis de renforcer l'éclairage de ces espaces urbains appelés à accueillir une importante circulation durant les Jeux. Lire aussi: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Quand la mode entre dans l’arène olympique L'entreprise a également participé à l'habillage lumineux de Dakar, avec la réalisation et l’installation d’Ayo géants, de décors lumineux sur les poteaux ainsi que d'arches lumineuses. À cela s'ajoutent des travaux d'installation de feux de signalisation tricolores sur l'avenue Blaise Diagne et les deux voies du Canal Fass. Ces différents chantiers ont mobilisé au moins 300 personnes, entre employés, stagiaires et alternants. Des profils issus de plusieurs spécialités ont ainsi pris part aux opérations, notamment dans les domaines des études techniques, du génie civil, de la maçonnerie, de la métallurgie et de la logistique. Une contribution qui illustre également la dimension économique et professionnelle des Joj, à travers la mobilisation de compétences et de ressources humaines locales. 200 000 points lumineux au Sénégal et dans la sous-région Si les Joj ont offert une nouvelle vitrine à son savoir-faire, Ert n'en est pas à sa première expérience dans les grands travaux d'infrastructures. Créée en 1991, l’entreprise sénégalaise s’est spécialisée dans l’étude, la réalisation et la maintenance des réseaux de distribution électrique, de l’éclairage public, des systèmes solaires photovoltaïques et des feux de signalisation tricolores. Elle intervient également dans l’aménagement des espaces publics. En 35 ans d’activité, la société revendique l’installation d’environ 200 000 points lumineux au Sénégal et dans la sous-région, ainsi que l’équipement de 75 carrefours en feux de signalisation tricolores. À Dakar, elle indique avoir installé environ 98 % du réseau d’éclairage public de la ville, dont elle assure l’entretien depuis 25 ans. Lire aussi: JOJ 2026 : Malang, Pape Aly et Aline, trois parcours au cœur d’une cérémonie historique Son portefeuille de réalisations comprend notamment l'éclairage du Port autonome de Dakar, celui du stade de Grand-Yoff et les installations d’éclairage public du Bus Rapid Transit (Brt). Dans le domaine du solaire, l’entreprise a également contribué à la solarisation de la cathédrale de Dakar et de la mosquée de Dieuppeul. Elle a par ailleurs réalisé des installations de lampadaires solaires dans plusieurs localités du pays, notamment à Thiès, Sédhiou, Louga, Saint-Louis, en Casamance et à Kédougou. Son expertise s'étend également au-delà des frontières sénégalaises, avec des installations de lampadaires solaires au Tchad. L'entreprise met également en avant ses certifications Iso 9001 et Iso 14001, obtenues en 2015, ainsi que la certification Iso 45001, acquise en 2018, respectivement relatives au management de la qualité, à la gestion environnementale et à la santé et la sécurité au travail. Au-delà de la réalisation des infrastructures, l’entreprise dit développer des solutions destinées à améliorer la gestion et la performance des réseaux d’éclairage public. Elle s’appuie également sur un laboratoire de test des équipements et une salle de supervision pour assurer le suivi de ses installations. Les Joj Dakar 2026 laissent ainsi apparaître une autre dimension de son héritage : celle des compétences nationales mobilisées pour relever le défi de l’organisation. Au-delà des médailles, des performances sportives et des images qui auront fait le tour du monde, la transformation des espaces urbains rappelle que le Sénégal dispose aussi d’entreprises et de ressources humaines capables de concevoir, de réaliser et d'entretenir des infrastructures répondant aux exigences des grands rendez-vous internationaux. S.G

items.title: Jinapor holds talks with US diplomats on Ghana-US cooperation
items.description: Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, has engaged a delegation from the United States Embassy in Accra, reaffirming the importance of sustained diplomatic cooperation between Ghana and the US. The delegation was led by outgoing Chargé d’Affaires, Rolf Olson, and included Faris Asad, who is set to take over the diplomatic position. The meeting offered Dr Jinapor an opportunity to interact with both officials as the transition in the embassy’s leadership approaches. In a Facebook post on Thursday, November 12, the Minister said the engagement provided a platform to discuss matters of mutual interest, identify common priorities and explore opportunities for closer collaboration. Dr Jinapor expressed appreciation to Mr Olson and wished him success in his future endeavours, while extending a warm welcome to Mr Asad. He said he looked forward to building on the existing relationship and advancing a stronger partnership between Ghana and the United States.

items.title: Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick
items.description: Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino expected to replace him. Former United midfielder Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are mired in the relegation zone. “Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach,” the club said in a statement. It added: “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.” Carrick’s final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away and was looking to the international break as usual. But the United hierarchy have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins in all competitions. Former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino would have an enormous task on his hands to revive a club that has never recovered from the departure of Alex Ferguson 13 years ago. The Red Devils, once the dominant force in English football, have been overtaken by Manchester City, Liverpool and Arsenal. United’s next game is against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. The post Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Inondations à Gaza : malgré le désastre, Israël bloque toujours l’aide humanitaire
items.description: Le supplice des habitants de Gaza n'est pas près de prendre fin. Alors que l’enclave palestinienne est presque entièrement dévastée par trois ans de bombardements israéliens, les pluies d'automne ont emporté les tentes des survivants. Le pire est peut-être à venir pendant l’hiver qui approche. Les Nations-unies tirent la sonnette d’alarme. Gaza : après les bombardements, les trombes d'eau emportent tout Les images des tentes de Gaza sous la pluie et les torrents sont choquantes. Ceux que la guerre a épargnés vivent dans des conditions inimaginables et Israël s’entête toujours à refuser de laisser passer l'aide humanitaire. Les premières estimations font état de plus de 200 000 personnes touchées par les inondations qui ont endommagé les abris de plus de 40 000 familles et fait de nombreux morts. Pour le SG adjoint et coordinateur des secours d'urgence des Nations-Unies, Tom Fletcher, il n’y a plus de temps à perdre. Le diplomate britannique a appelé à ouvrir tous les points de passage vers Gaza et à mobiliser immédiatement les efforts de l'ensemble de la communauté humanitaire afin de répondre adéquatement aux besoins de la population civile de Gaza pendant l'hiver qui s'approche. “Des vies perdues, une population à nouveau en grand danger” “Fini les retards. Fini les excuses. Nous devons ouvrir tous les points de passage, mobiliser l'ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et mettre en œuvre l'intégralité de notre plan hivernal pour Gaza”, a-t-il écrit mercredi sur X. Fletcher a expliqué que pendant des mois, il lui a été expliqué que “des progrès seraient difficiles” avant les élections israéliennes. Maintenant que les élections sont passées, l’argument avancé c'est d'attendre la formation d'un gouvernement. “Au cas où quelqu'un aurait des doutes sur le droit international humanitaire : ce n'est pas une excuse acceptable”, a signifié le diplomate. Les conséquences des retards, des blocages et des coupes budgétaires sont “des vies perdues, une population à nouveau en grand danger”, a-t-il dénoncé. Ce qui rend la situation “encore plus exaspérante”, c'est que les Gazaouis courent ce “risque inutile” face à des conditions météorologiques qui “ne constituent pas une menace là où il existe un abri décent”. “Mettez fin à cette punition collective !” Les inondations ne constitueraient pas une telle menace si la communauté internationale avait été “en mesure de fournir des tentes décentes et des équipements d'hiver essentiels” et si les Palestiniens “avaient été autorisés à accéder à des zones ouvertes moins sujettes aux inondations”, écrit Tom Fletcher. Les besoins de la population de Gaza pendant l’hiver ont été pourtant établis il y a plusieurs semaines. Des abris durables, des vêtements chauds, des couvertures, de la literie, des solutions de chauffage sûres, des générateurs, du carburant, de l'huile moteur, des pièces de rechange, du matériel pour pomper l'eau, enlever les débris et déminer, égrène le haut responsable onusien. Fletcher a conclu par ce cri d'alarme : “Plus de retard. Ouvrez tous les points de passage, pas seulement un. Laissez nos partenaires ONG travailler. Permettez aux marchés commerciaux de fonctionner. Mettez fin à cette punition collective. Financez le plan. Mettez fin à ces souffrances prévisibles et évitables. Le monde n'est pas impuissant.” L’article Inondations à Gaza : malgré le désastre, Israël bloque toujours l’aide humanitaire est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Weak death records and poor health data systems threaten timely healthcare in Africa – WHO
items.description: Weak systems for recording deaths, tracking health needs and analysing reliable health information could delay lifesaving interventions, leave preventable health risks undetected and make it harder for communities to access essential healthcare, the World Health Organisation (WHO) has warned. A new WHO assessment of 40 countries in the African Region has revealed significant weaknesses in the health information systems governments depend on to establish why people are dying, identify emerging health threats and direct healthcare services and resources to communities that need them most. One of the most concerning findings is the limited capacity of countries to record deaths and establish their causes. Only 19 of the 40 countries assessed reported notifying authorities of at least 80% of deaths, while 21 reported recording the cause of death for at least 80% of registered deaths. The gaps could make it difficult for health authorities to identify recurring causes of preventable mortality, recognise weaknesses in healthcare delivery and take timely action to protect vulnerable populations. When deaths are not adequately documented and their causes established, governments risk losing important information needed to understand mortality patterns and determine where interventions are most urgently required. Weak capacity to analyse and use health information The report, The Maturity and Functionality of Health Information System in the WHO African Region , also highlights weaknesses in countries’ ability to turn collected health information into reliable evidence for decision-making. Only 43% of the countries assessed reported having sufficient capacity to analyse health data at health facility level, while just 25% reported sufficient capacity at that level to assess data quality. This means that even where health facilities collect information, inadequate analytical skills and data-quality assessment systems could limit the ability of health managers to identify service delivery gaps, monitor emerging health risks and determine where additional healthcare workers, equipment and other resources are required. WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, said countries needed to move beyond collecting health information and ensure that it informed decisions and interventions. “When we do not know why people are dying, which children are missing essential services or where communities face the greatest health risks, we may overlook the very people who need our attention most. Countries have made important progress in collecting health data, but information must lead to action. We need stronger investment, skilled professionals and better coordination to turn reliable information into decisions that prevent avoidable deaths, improve healthcare and reach the most vulnerable communities,” he said. African health information systems score 59% in maturity assessment The assessment, conducted in 2024 across 40 of the WHO African Region’s 47 Member States, gave the countries an overall health information system maturity score of 59 out of 100. The score indicates that many countries remain at an early stage in developing the systems and institutional capacities required to produce, analyse and effectively use reliable health information. However, country scores ranged from 26 to 93, reflecting considerable differences in progress across the region and the need for approaches that respond to individual countries’ circumstances. Financing and governance emerged as major constraints to strengthening these systems. Only 18% of the countries assessed reported having a dedicated budget line for health information systems, while 35% had an up-to-date national policy to guide their development. The report also identified weaknesses in coordination, routine data-quality checks and the availability of trained professionals. These challenges could undermine the sustainability of health information systems and limit the ability of governments to translate investments in data collection and management into improvements in healthcare delivery. Digital reporting advances, but patient records remain limited Despite the institutional and technical challenges, countries have made progress in adopting digital platforms for routine health reporting. Forty-three of the WHO African Region’s 47 Member States have adopted a digital platform for collecting and reporting routine health information. However, the adoption of digital reporting platforms has not translated into widespread implementation of digital patient medical records. Only 20% of the countries participating in the assessment reported implementing digital patient medical records, while fewer than half had established frameworks that allow different health information systems to exchange information. This lack of interoperability means information generated by hospitals, laboratories and other health services can remain disconnected, making it difficult for health authorities to develop a comprehensive understanding of people’s health needs and plan healthcare services effectively. Zimbabwe and Nigeria demonstrate the value of reliable health data Country experiences highlighted in the report demonstrate how improved health information systems can help authorities identify gaps and take practical action. In Zimbabwe, maternal and perinatal death reporting previously depended on paper-based records that could take weeks or months to reach decision-makers. The delays affected the timely identification of preventable risks, highlighting the importance of systems that allow critical health information to reach the people responsible for making decisions. In Nigeria’s Bauchi State, health authorities used vaccination data and community-level information to identify children who had missed routine immunisation and target communities that were underserved. The examples illustrate how accessible and reliable information can support more targeted health interventions and help authorities identify populations that might otherwise be overlooked. WHO launches Regional Health Data Hub to strengthen information systems WHO and countries are taking steps to address the identified weaknesses. In August 2026, WHO launched the Regional Health Data Hub, a digital platform designed to bring together information from different health programmes and provide a more comprehensive picture of population health. The platform is intended to make health information easier to access, analyse and compare, enabling decision-makers to identify underserved populations, monitor health trends and direct resources to where they are most needed. The initiative forms part of broader efforts to strengthen the availability and use of health information across the African Region. The findings were presented at the opening of the First Africa Health Data Forum in Nairobi, Kenya, on 10 November 2026. The three-day forum, running from 10 to 12 November, brings together Ministers of Health, senior government officials, WHO and development partners to examine the findings, share country experiences and identify practical solutions and investment priorities for strengthening health information systems. Discussions are expected to focus on common and country-specific challenges, opportunities for coordinated investment and the practical actions required to improve the collection, management and use of health information. Participants will also examine how digital health, artificial intelligence and other innovations can strengthen health information systems and support more responsive healthcare services. The findings of the assessment are expected to inform these discussions as countries and partners explore ways to address weaknesses in health data governance, financing, infrastructure and technical capacity.

items.title: Kenya calls for African-led health data systems as 51 countries gather in Nairobi
items.description: Kenya has called for African countries to take greater ownership of their health information systems, warning against fragmented digital platforms, duplicated investments and dependence on technologies developed outside the continent. Kenya’s Cabinet Secretary for Health, Aden Duale, made the call on 10 November 2026 when he officially opened the First Africa Health Data Forum in Nairobi. “For Kenya, digitisation and data are not simple enablers. They are the backbone of our universal health coverage,” he said. The three-day forum, running until 12 November under the theme “Better Data, Better Health for All” , is convened by the World Health Organisation (WHO), the Kenya Digital Health Agency and Kenya’s Ministry of Health. It has brought together more than 300 participants from 51 countries across the WHO African and Eastern Mediterranean regions, including government representatives, development partners, academics, civil society organisations and private-sector innovators. The meeting is providing a platform for countries to share experiences, identify priorities and explore practical solutions for strengthening health information systems. Health data are essential for understanding why people are dying, identifying emerging health threats and determining where healthcare services and resources are most urgently needed. Kenya pushes for a unified patient health record Addressing participants, Mr Duale outlined Kenya’s ambition to bring patients’ health information together through a unified digital system. “So our vision is very simple: one patient, one longitudinal health record, which is accessible wherever that patient receives care,” he said. He cautioned that declining external financing made it increasingly important for African countries to avoid fragmented systems and unnecessary duplication of investments. “However, as external financing shrinks, Africa cannot afford fragmented systems, cannot afford parallel reporting and duplicated investments. Every dollar and every shilling must strengthen our national health information system,” he said. The Cabinet Secretary also announced plans to establish a National Intelligence and Analytics Centre under the Digital Health Agency to strengthen the analysis of health data. He emphasised the importance of timely information in healthcare decision-making, saying: “What gets measured is managed, and what gets measured in real time, we can act in real time.” Mr Duale further challenged African countries to develop their own technological solutions rather than remain dependent on innovations produced elsewhere. “However, Africa should not merely be a consumer of technologies developed elsewhere. We must become producers of solutions that respond to our own priorities and realities,” he said. Kenya’s Ebola response demonstrates the value of health data WHO Regional Director for Africa, Professor Mohamed Yakub Janabi, highlighted Kenya’s response to Bundibugyo Ebola Virus as an example of how reliable information can support public health interventions. He said Kenya traced all 135 contacts of its first case, both within the country and internationally, while the eight contacts who subsequently tested positive were already in quarantine. The experience, he said, demonstrated the importance of ensuring that information reaches the people responsible for taking action. “Data did not replace people. It told people where to go, whom to call, and when,” Professor Janabi said. “Good data turns alarms into actions. That only happens when the right information reaches the right people at the right time. Kenya has shown us what is possible when data and decisive actions meet,” he added. His remarks highlighted the relationship between effective health information systems, disease surveillance and the ability of authorities to respond to public health threats. WHO report exposes weaknesses in African health information systems At the opening ceremony, Professor Janabi launched a new WHO report, The Maturity and Functionality of Health Information Systems in the WHO African Region . The assessment, conducted in 2024 across 40 of the Region’s 47 Member States, gave health information systems an overall maturity score of 59 out of 100. The findings indicate that many countries in the WHO African Region remain at an early stage in developing the systems and capacities needed to produce and use reliable health information. The report’s launch brought attention to the need for stronger investment, institutional capacity and coordination to ensure that health information supports effective healthcare planning and delivery. Director of Programme Management at the WHO Regional Office for Africa, Dr Abdourahmane Diallo, stressed that reliable information was also necessary to ensure accountability in public spending. “A budget allocation is a commitment to the public. Governments need credible evidence of whether funding was used as intended and what it achieved,” he said. He emphasised the importance of credible data in assessing whether health investments are delivering the intended results. WHO’s efforts to strengthen access to health information across the continent also featured prominently at the forum. In August 2026, the organisation launched the Regional Health Data Hub, a digital platform designed to bring together information from different health programmes in one place. The platform is intended to strengthen access to health information and support more effective decision-making by countries. Dr Benson Droti of the WHO Regional Office for Africa demonstrated how the platform works during the forum. He clarified that the platform was developed for the benefit of Member States rather than as a WHO-owned system. “It is not the WHO’s platform. It’s a platform built for the member states,” he said. The initiative reflects efforts to make health information more accessible and useful to national authorities responsible for planning and managing healthcare services. In a video message, WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also emphasised the importance of African ownership and governance of health information. “Crucially, Africa’s health data must be owned, governed, and used by African countries in the interests of their people,” he said. WHO and development partners call for country-led action In her welcome remarks, Dr Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo, WHO Representative to Kenya, said the forum should produce practical action rather than another set of recommendations. “The aim of this Forum is not another set of recommendations. It is to listen to countries and act together, and WHO stands ready to align our support behind country priorities,” she said. Development partners also highlighted the importance of ensuring that health information captures the needs of vulnerable populations, particularly children. UNICEF Regional Director for Eastern and Southern Africa, Etleva Kadilli, said, “For UNICEF, behind every data, there is a child.” Chief of Staff of the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, Aboubakri Diaw, similarly stressed the consequences of failing to account for every child in national planning. “A child who is not counted is a child who is not planned for,” he said. Forum seeks practical roadmap for Africa’s health data systems With two days of discussions remaining, countries and partners are expected to examine the changes needed to strengthen health information systems and translate national priorities into coordinated action. The discussions will focus on identifying common challenges, aligning partner support with country priorities and developing plans for follow-up. The forum is also expected to become a biennial meeting, providing an opportunity for countries to review progress every two years. Closing his opening remarks, Kenya’s Cabinet Secretary for Health, Mr Duale, called for the meeting to produce concrete commitments and clearly defined responsibilities. “Let us leave Nairobi with a very practical Africa Health Data Roadmap,” he said. Adding that, “Let us leave Nairobi with a country-partner alignment matrix, with very clear responsibilities, clear timelines, and a way to track delivery.”

items.title: Goumeri W-8 : le Niger accélère la riposte face à une éruption pétrolière majeure à Agadem…
items.description: Le ministère du Pétrole et celui de l’Environnement, de l’Hydraulique et de l’Assainissement ont rendu public, le mardi après-midi, un communiqué conjoint sur l’éruption du puits Goumeri W-8, situé dans le bloc pétrolier d’Agadem, dans la région de Diffa. Présenté par Abdoul Karim Mohamed Ali, Secrétaire général du ministère du Pétrole, le document apporte des précisions sur l’évolution de l’incident et sur les mesures engagées pour le maîtriser. L’éruption, survenue le 25 septembre 2026, a provoqué des projections de pétrole brut et de gaz depuis le puits Goumeri W-8, exploité par CNPC Niger Petroleum S.A. Les autorités ont qualifié la situation d’incident environnemental de gravité exceptionnelle, mobilisant les services techniques afin de sécuriser le site, contenir les déversements et reprendre le contrôle du puits. Selon les informations rendues publiques, le déversement de pétrole brut a été contenu, tandis que les opérations techniques se poursuivent sur le terrain. La priorité est désormais la réalisation d’un puits de secours directionnel, baptisé Goumeri W-8R, destiné à permettre la neutralisation définitive de l’éruption. Les travaux de forage de ce puits de secours devraient s’étendre du 24 octobre au 26 décembre 2026. Cette opération constitue l’élément central de la stratégie des autorités pour maîtriser durablement l’incident et prévenir toute aggravation des conséquences environnementales dans la zone d’Agadem. Le gouvernement a également sollicité l’expertise algérienne, avec la venue d’une mission technique composée de cadres du ministère des Hydrocarbures, de l’Autorité de régulation des hydrocarbures et du groupe Sonatrach. Cette coopération vise à renforcer l’évaluation de la situation et l’identification de solutions techniques appropriées. À ce stade, les autorités assurent que la situation reste sous surveillance et que les équipes spécialisées travaillent jour et nuit sur le site. Le communiqué conjoint vise ainsi à rassurer les populations et à préciser l’état d’avancement des opérations, alors que la maîtrise totale de l’éruption demeure l’objectif prioritaire. L’article Goumeri W-8 : le Niger accélère la riposte face à une éruption pétrolière majeure à Agadem… est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

items.title: E-sport : avec son guide national, la Guinée se met aux standards internationaux
items.description: En publiant le Guide national d'organisation d'événement e-sport, la FNEG pose une pierre de plus dans la structuration de la discipline et affirme l'ambition de la Guinée sur la scène e-sportive africaine. Officiellement reconnue par l'État et affiliée à la World Esports Federation, la FNEG poursuit son travail de structuration de l'e-sport guinéen. Après la mise en place de son cadre institutionnel, la Fédération se dote d'un référentiel national pour l'organisation des événements, un outil dont disposent déjà les nations e-sportives les plus avancées. Ce guide s'adresse à tous les acteurs : organisateurs privés, clubs, salles de jeu, mais aussi partenaires, sponsors et institutions publiques appelés à soutenir des événements. Il établit un langage commun et des exigences partagées. C'est une condition pour que la Guinée puisse accueillir des compétitions d'envergure. « La Fédération ambitionne d'accueillir dès 2027 des événements internationaux d'e-sport à Conakry. » Le Président de la FNEG, M. Malian THIAM et son équipe, place cette publication dans une vision à long terme : « Une fédération se juge à la qualité de ses compétitions. Si nous voulons que la Guinée soit respectée par les instances internationales et choisie pour accueillir de grands événements, nous devons d'abord être exemplaires chez nous. Ce guide est notre engagement en ce sens. Je demande à toutes les parties prenantes, publiques comme privées, d'en faire la référence de tout événement e-sport en Guinée. » La FNEG invite les partenaires et institutions à s'appuyer sur ce guide pour évaluer les projets d'événements qui leur sont soumis. Le guide est disponible le lien ci-dessous : https://www.esports-guinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Guide-National-dEsports-Guinee.pdf L’article E-sport : avec son guide national, la Guinée se met aux standards internationaux est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Carrick sacked as Manchester United head coach
items.description: Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United head coach, with Mauricio Pochettino lined up to replace him. Carrick departs less than six months after signing a two-year contract, having overseen the club’s worst-ever start to a Premier League season with United in the relegation zone after picking up one win in 10 matches. United have an agreement in place with Pochettino to take over, but he is likely to remain in charge of the USA for their Nations League against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday before starting work. Pochettino has a £7m release clause in his newly-signed contract with the USA. Talks with the United Soccer Federation are expected to gather pace in the coming days. Carrick took training in Manchester on Wednesday as United reached a verbal agreement with Pochettino. Meanwhile, club chiefs were at a Monaco summit with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. That is where the decision to sack Carrick was ratified by Ratcliffe following the recommendation of chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick’s exit follows United’s 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, when they fell 2-0 down inside four minutes and then 4-2 down early in the second half before mounting a last-gasp comeback to draw. The rescue job followed a similar turnaround to beat Roma in the Champions League last Tuesday but was not enough to convince the United hierarchy to continue with the former midfielder in charge. Carrick was initially appointed as United boss in January 2026 on a contract until the end of the season, following Ruben Amorim’s sacking earlier in that campaign. He delivered a brilliant run of results, winning 12 of 17 matches to earn a third-place finish in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. Carrick was nominated for Premier League Manager of the Season and, on May 22, signed a new contract running to 2028. However, just three wins in 15 matches this term have cost him his job. United are now looking for an eighth permanent head coach since Sir Alex Ferguson left in 2013 – with Pochettino understood to be ready to take the role. Former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino has been considered for the United job on three previous occasions, but finally now looks set for the Old Trafford hot seat.

items.title: Lutte contre le trafic de stupéfiants : La Police Nationale saisit plus de 300 kg de cannabis à Ouagadougou
items.description: Dans le cadre de l’exécution de l’opération WIBGA 3, le Commissariat de Police de District (CPD) de Saaba, conjointement avec la Compagnie Républicaine de la Sécurité (CRS) de Ouagadougou, ont réussi à saisir, lors d’une mission de contrôle dans la capitale, une importante quantité de cannabis. En effet, dans le cadre de l’opération WIBGA 3, des équipes du CPD-Saaba et de la CRS-Ouaga ont été déployées dans les différents carrefours et les zones criminogènes de la commune de Saaba. C’est ainsi que, sur la Route Nationale n° 04 (axe Ouaga-Fada), à hauteur de la voie de contournement, les éléments ont intercepté un tricycle transportant trois (03) sacs et demi de 100 kg (soit environ 350 kg) de cannabis. Les investigations vont par la suite permettre aux enquêteurs d’appréhender le suspect principal. Le mode opératoire consistait à faire transporter, depuis un pays étranger, le cannabis déjà conditionné dans des emballages à destination du Burkina Faso. Le transport se faisait à travers les chauffeurs de camion qui prenaient soin de bien camoufler le produit dans leurs véhicules pour ne pas se faire interpeller par les forces de l’ordre au cours de leur trajet. Une fois le colis arrivé à Ouagadougou, il était récupéré et vendu en gros aux clients, puis effectuaient leurs transactions en numéraire via Orange Money et autres. Les personnes impliquées dans ce business évitaient au maximum de laisser des traces pouvant permettre de les identifier facilement. La Police Nationale remercie les citoyens qui ont permis d’atteindre ce résultat et, par là, tous ceux qui ne ménagent aucun effort pour accompagner la Police Nationale et l’ensemble des forces de sécurité dans la lutte contre l’insécurité sous toutes ses formes. Elle les invite à toujours continuer de dénoncer les cas suspects aux numéros verts que sont les 17, 16 et 1010. La Police Nationale, une force publique au service des citoyens !

items.title: Two policemen, including ASI, martyred in attack on patrolling party in Swabi: DPO
items.description: SWABI: Two policemen, including an assistant sub-inspector (ASI) heading the Mansori police post, were martyred when three suspects opened fire on a patrolling party on Wednesday night, District Police Officer Waqas Rafiq told the media. DPO Rafiq said another policeman was critically injured in the attack. Constable Nawab Ali said the police received information that ASI Walid Khan, who was in charge of the Mansori police post, and his team had come under attack while on patrol. The nearby police station was subsequently informed, and personnel reached the scene, where they found Head Constable Shahid Khan, 28, injured. In his statement to the police, Shahid said that when the patrolling party reached India Cham in the Gohati area, ASI Walid was sitting in the front seat of the vehicle, while he and other policemen were seated in the back. He said they spotted three armed suspects carrying Kalashnikovs and pistols, whom they identified in the vehicle’s headlights. The suspects are reportedly all residents of the area. “We got out of the vehicle,” Shahid said, adding that the police party attempted to arrest the suspects, but they tried to evade capture. The suspects then opened fire on the policemen in an attempt to escape, killing ASI Walid and Constable Zulfiqar on the spot and critically injuring Shahid, he said. Meanwhile, the funeral prayers of ASI Walid and Constable Zulfiqar were offered with full official honours at Police Lines, Shahmansoor, Swabi, on Wednesday. Mardan Regional Police Officer Qasim Ali Khan, DPO Waqas Rafiq, other police officials and relatives of the deceased attended the funeral prayers. On Wednesday, 10 police personnel were martyred when a police team came under attack while returning from an operation against elements involved in illegal gold mining. Police station came under attack In a separate incident, terrorists attacked the Bandkorai Police Station in Dera Ismail Khan on Wednesday night by ramming an explosives-laden pickup into its main gate, triggering a powerful blast followed by intense gunfire. However, prompt retaliatory fire by police personnel prevented the attackers from entering the police station, forcing them to flee. All police personnel present inside the station remained safe, and no casualties were reported. The powerful blast destroyed the station’s main gate and brought down part of its boundary wall. A nearby mosque was also destroyed, while several houses in the surrounding area were damaged, with their windowpanes shattered by the force of the explosion. Soon after the attack, additional police personnel and security forces arrived at the scene, cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to track down the attackers.

items.title: Maisons de la jeunesse : 37,4 milliards de FCFA et des retards persistants dans les chantiers
items.description: Malgré un financement global de 37,42 milliards de FCFA de la Banque d’investissement et de développement de la CEDEAO (BIDC), le programme de construction des Maisons de la jeunesse et de la citoyenneté (MJC) affiche des retards importants. Sur les 38 infrastructures prévues dans sa deuxième phase, seules sept sont déclarées finalisées en 2026. Le ministère de la Jeunesse et des Sports prévoit néanmoins de poursuivre leur réalisation en 2027. Le programme des Maisons de la jeunesse et de la citoyenneté (MJC) connaît des difficultés d'exécution. C'est l'un des principaux constats qui ressort du rapport de présentation du projet de budget 2027 du ministère de la Jeunesse et des Sports. Alors que ces infrastructures sont présentées comme des espaces destinés à accueillir des activités sportives, culturelles, socio-économiques, environnementales et sanitaires, leur réalisation accuse des retards dans plusieurs localités du pays. Le bilan de la première phase du programme illustre ces difficultés. Sur les huit départements concernés – Pikine, Guédiawaye, Matam, Podor, Kaolack, Fatick, Goudiry et Vélingara –, seule la Maison de la jeunesse de Kaolack a été réceptionnée. Le ministère évoque des lenteurs et des défaillances d'entreprises qui ont entraîné des résiliations de contrats et des arrêts de travaux. Ces situations ont même nécessité la saisine de l'Agent judiciaire de l'État. Les difficultés ne concernent pas uniquement les entreprises. Certains chantiers repris connaissent des niveaux d'avancement inégaux, en raison notamment de problèmes d'approbation des contrats par la Direction centrale des marchés publics (DCMP), de non-immatriculation de marchés par le ministère des Finances et du Budget ou encore de déficits de financement. La deuxième phase, qui concerne 38 départements et bénéficie d'un financement global de 37,42 milliards de FCFA de la BIDC, présente également des niveaux d'exécution contrastés. Selon le bilan arrêté en 2026, sept infrastructures sont finalisées, quatre affichent un taux d'avancement supérieur à 80 %, tandis que dix se situent entre 60 et 80 %. Dix autres présentent un niveau d'exécution compris entre 10 et 60 %. Enfin, sept chantiers n'ont pas encore démarré. Face à cette situation, le département entend maintenir le programme parmi ses priorités pour l'exercice 2027. Dans le projet de budget soumis à l'examen des députés, une enveloppe de 5,398 milliards de FCFA est prévue pour la construction des Maisons de la jeunesse et de la citoyenneté. Le ministère annonce notamment la finalisation des infrastructures relevant de la deuxième phase. Au total, le projet de budget 2027 du ministère de la Jeunesse et des Sports s'établit à 35,327 milliards de FCFA, contre 40,316 milliards en 2026, soit une baisse de 12,37 %. Cette diminution est principalement imputée à la fin des engagements financiers de l'État en faveur du Comité d'organisation des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (COJOJ) Dakar 2026. Au-delà des annonces budgétaires, l'enjeu demeure désormais celui de l'exécution. Pour les jeunes des départements concernés, la livraison effective de ces infrastructures constitue une condition essentielle pour accéder aux espaces d'accompagnement, de formation, de loisirs et d'engagement citoyen promis par le programme. Cheikh Tidiane NDIAYE

items.title: L’Égypte confirme le déploiement de soldats en Arabie saoudite
items.description: Des militaires egyptiens sont stationnes en Arabie saoudite depuis des mois. Le ministre egyptien des Affaires etrangeres, Badr Abdelatty, l'a confirme dans un entretien a France 24 paru le 9 novembre, precisant que Le Caire renforcait sa presence a la demande de Riyad. Cette annonce officialise un engagement militaire jusque-la discret, sur fond de nouvelles attaques des rebelles houthis contre le royaume. La mission est « essentiellement defensive », assure le chef de la diplomatie. Elle vise a proteger les sites sensibles, notamment les lieux saints de La Mecque et de Medine, ainsi qu'a etoffer les capacites de defense antiaerienne saoudiennes. Abdelatty exclut toute operation de l'armee egyptienne au Yemen. Selon The Nationa l, qui cite des sources informees, plusieurs centaines de soldats auraient ete envoyes avec des blindes, des batteries sol-air et des missiles. Aucun effectif n'a toutefois ete communique officiellement. Riyad en quete de soutien La confirmation vient a la suite de l'autorisation donnee le 26 octobre par le Parlement egyptien au president Abdel Fattah al-Sissi pour soutenir militairement l'Arabie saoudite. Le ministre precise neanmoins que les premieres forces etaient deja presentes avant ce vote, apres les attaques subies par le royaume pendant l'escalade avec l'Iran. Depuis la reprise des hostilites au Yemen, les Houthis, soutenus par Teheran, ont multiplie les tirs de drones et de missiles vers les infrastructures petrolieres et aeroportuaires saoudiennes. Une partie du mouvement avait denonce le feu vert du Parlement comme une « declaration de guerre ». Le Caire insiste au contraire sur son refus d'ouvrir un nouveau front et affirme poursuivre ses efforts de mediation. Au-dela de la protection du territoire saoudien, ce deploiement illustre le resserrement de la cooperation securitaire entre Le Caire et Riyad, alors que les monarchies du Golfe renforcent leurs defenses face aux menaces regionales.

items.title: 'Significant evidence' of placer gold in Punjab rivers, says CM Maryam at minerals investment forum
items.description: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said on Thursday that there was “significant evidence” of “sufficient quantities” of placer gold flowing in the province’s five rivers. She was speaking at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum in Islamabad, an initiative aimed at harnessing the country’s mineral resources and attracting domestic and foreign investment in the mining sector. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also addressed the event, which was attended by the chief ministers of Balochistan and Sindh, as well as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. Maryam said Punjab was the land of five rivers and that gold was “literally flowing” in all five, particularly in the areas of Mianwali and Attock. Describing Pakistan as a “pot of gold”, she said its wealth lay both above and beneath the ground and needed to be explored and converted into tangible wealth. “The wealth beneath Punjab was never a problem, never a problem, just like the whole of Pakistan, just like all four provinces and the federating units. The chaos above ground was the actual problem,” she said. Maryam said the provincial mines and minerals department’s revenue stood at around Rs10 billion two and a half years ago but had since increased to Rs40bn. “And it is just the beginning,” she added. She also highlighted the province’s iron ore reserves, saying Chiniot had 261.5 million tonnes of iron ore. She said the provincial government was taking steps to facilitate investment in the mining sector and create an enabling environment for investors. The Punjab chief minister said her role as chief executive of the country’s most populous province was to facilitate investors and create an enabling environment by eliminating red tape, bureaucratic delays and unnecessary hurdles. The provincial government was offering one-window facilitation to ensure investors did not have to run from pillar to post to complete the necessary procedures, she added. Maryam said the government was also making substantial capital investments to reduce investors’ capital expenditure and prevent them from having to tie up funds in purchasing expensive land. Additionally, the government was offering concessional financing of up to Rs5 billion and would provide solar-powered energy solutions to investors to help offset high energy and fuel costs. Dar says provincial partnership vital for mineral development Dar said Pakistan’s constitutional framework made provincial partnership indispensable, adding that the provinces were essential partners in the national undertaking and that their constitutional authority and ownership of mineral resources must be respected. Addressing the event, he said the federal government was working alongside provincial governments and their leadership through national coordination, investment facilitation, policy alignment and international engagement. Dar said Pakistan’s mineral resources were central to the next phase of the country’s economic transformation, stressing the need to diversify exports, strengthen the industrial base and attract long-term investment. He said Pakistan possessed substantial and diverse mineral resources, including significant copper and gold potential along the Tethyan metallogenic belt in the west of the country. The country also had deposits of iron ore, chromite, lead, zinc, coal, rock salt, marble, gypsum, gemstones and other industrial minerals. The deputy PM said the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan demonstrated the potential of international expertise, national participation and provincial ownership in attracting major long-term investment. He stressed that Pakistan’s ambition should extend beyond extracting minerals and exporting them in raw form, saying the country needed to develop the capacity to process and refine them, as well as manufacture mineral-based products domestically. Dar said Balochistan was central to Pakistan’s mineral future, adding that the development of its resources should contribute meaningfully to the provincial economy and the well-being of its people. He also emphasised the importance of local employment, skills development and the participation of Pakistani companies, saying local communities must be active participants in and beneficiaries of mineral development. The deputy prime minister further stated that environmental protection, workers’ safety and the rehabilitation of mining sites were essential to a successful minerals industry. The Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan is one of Pakistan’s most ambitious mining ventures, with significant potential to boost the country’s mineral wealth through the extraction of gold and copper. Designed as an open-pit mining and processing operation , the project will initially process 45 million tonnes of ore annually, with capacity expected to double to 90m tonnes after the completion of Phase 2. The mine has an estimated operational life of 37 years, which could potentially extend to 80 years through further exploration and resource development.
