items.title: IA dans dans l’enseignement supérieur : Vers un cadre national pour harmoniser les usages dans les universités
items.description: L’Académie nationale des sciences et techniques du Sénégal (Ansts) a ouvert, hier, à Dakar, un atelier de deux jours consacré à l’intégration de l’intelligence artificielle (IA) dans l’enseignement supérieur. L’objectif est de parvenir à un cadre national harmonisé pour encadrer les usages de cette technologie, renforcer les compétences des acteurs universitaires et améliorer les pratiques pédagogiques. L’utilisation croissante de l’intelligence artificielle générative dans les universités sénégalaises appelle désormais la mise en place de règles communes. C’est l’une des principales préoccupations soulevées, hier à Dakar, lors de l’ouverture de l’atelier de co-construction sur l’harmonisation des usages et l’intégration de l’IA dans l’enseignement supérieur et la recherche. Organisée par l’Académie nationale des sciences et techniques du Sénégal (Ansts), cette rencontre réunit des universitaires, des chercheurs, des experts et des acteurs de l’écosystème numérique. Représentant le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation, Dr Boubacar Camara, le Pr Elhadj Babacar Ly, directeur de l’innovation, de la valorisation, de la propriété intellectuelle et du transfert technologique, a insisté sur l’urgence d’encadrer les pratiques. Selon lui, l’intelligence artificielle générative s’est imposée en moins de trois ans comme un outil quotidien pour les enseignants, les étudiants et le personnel administratif, sans que les dispositifs réglementaires et pédagogiques aient suivi cette évolution. « Nous sommes dans un usage sans cadre », a-t-il relevé, soulignant que les opportunités offertes par cette technologie s’accompagnent de risques liés à l’intégrité académique, à la qualité des formations, à l’équité d’accès et à la protection des données personnelles. Pour le représentant du ministre, la réponse ne consiste ni à interdire cette technologie ni à laisser prospérer des pratiques incontrôlées. « Notre responsabilité est claire : ne subir ni interdire, mais encadrer et former », a-t-il déclaré. Le Pr Elhadj Babacar Ly a identifié quatre insuffisances majeures : l'absence de politiques explicites dans les établissements, le déficit de compétences certifiées, la dispersion des initiatives et la dépendance aux plateformes étrangères. Cette dernière soulève notamment des préoccupations relatives aux coûts, à la souveraineté numérique et à la valorisation des langues nationales. Il a ainsi plaidé pour l’élaboration d’un guide national des usages de l’IA générative, d’un référentiel de compétences et d’un programme de formation des formateurs. Le représentant du ministre a également annoncé que le Sénégal travaille à la mise en place d’un centre national d’intelligence artificielle à Diamniadio, dans le cadre de la coopération avec la Corée. Il a assuré que le ministère accordera une attention particulière aux conclusions de l’atelier et accompagnera leur mise en œuvre. Pour le Pr Moussa Lo, membre titulaire de l’Ansts, cette rencontre doit permettre de dépasser les initiatives individuelles afin de construire une approche cohérente à l’échelle nationale. « L’objectif de cet atelier, c’est vraiment de contribuer à l’élaboration d’un cadre harmonisé pour l’intégration de l’intelligence artificielle dans notre système d’enseignement supérieur », a-t-il expliqué. Selon l’académicien, l’utilisation de l’IA générative est déjà largement répandue dans les universités, aussi bien chez les étudiants que chez les enseignants et le personnel administratif. Cependant, l’absence d’encadrement favorise les abus et empêche une exploitation optimale de ses potentialités. Évoquant les enquêtes réalisées auprès des acteurs universitaires, notamment celle conduite par l’Unchk, le Pr Moussa Lo a indiqué que les premiers constats révèlent une utilisation importante de l’IA dans la préparation des cours, les évaluations et la rédaction de rapports. Ces travaux permettent également de mieux cerner les besoins en compétences et les attentes des utilisateurs. Il a toutefois précisé que l’harmonisation recherchée ne signifie pas l’uniformisation des pratiques. Elle doit plutôt permettre aux établissements de disposer de références communes tout en préservant leurs spécificités. Daouda DIOUF

items.title: Who could potentially replace Jensen Huang if Nvidia ousts him?
items.description: Chip giant Nvidia’s board was reportedly meeting Wednesday to discuss the future of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after he dated an accused Chinese spy, according to US media. The 63-year-old tech titan, who has led the key AI giant since it was founded in 1993, has been beleaguered with reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a data center executive who has been accused by US intelligence of working for China’s Ministry of State Security. With Huang unexpectedly on the backfoot, and no known plan of succession at Nvidia, the field is wide open for a variety of replacements to lead one of the key AI players should the board decide to oust Huang. Here are some of the names being suggested most frequently as Huang’s potential successor. Internal hire With over 40,000 employees, Nvidia could opt to go with an in-house pick to take the helm, including one of Huang’s dozens of direct reports. Tech publications frequently cited Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as an easy choice, if for no other reason than she is already among top leadership at the chip behemoth. Another longtime Nvidia honcho is Ian Buck, who oversees the company’s data center clients. He was a key mind behind the software that keeps Nvidia-designed chips in demand. Business magazine Inc. also lists Nvidia’s vice president of applied deep learning research, Bryan Catanzaro, as a possible pick. A family affair Huang could also try and position a member of his own family as his replacement, with more than one option for a bloodline succession. His daughter Madison Huang is currently the senior director of product marketing at Nvidia and is among the names most suggested by analysts. As a marketing leader, she had a multi-year stint at luxury conglomerate LVMH. Jensen Huang’s son Spencer Huang could also be a potential successor. He currently works at Nvidia as the director of product management in the company’s robotics division. Huang’s cousin, Lisa Su, could also be a viable candidate for selection – not only is she his first cousin, once removed, but she also has valuable expertise as the longtime CEO of semiconductor giant AMD. Tech CEO swap Su is not the only tech chief being bandied around as a possible replacement for Huang. Rene Haas, CEO of UK chip design firm Arm, is another candidate being suggested by the tech press. Speculation runs wide in Silicon Valley, where former Apple CEO Tim Cook – who stepped down from leading the tech giant in August after 15 years at the helm – is another person insiders say could potentially be tapped. items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : le Sénégal en quête de nouvelles finales en beach handball et taekwondo
items.description: Quinze titres seront en jeu ce jeudi 12 novembre, à l’occasion de l’avant-dernière journée des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Le Sénégal sera particulièrement attendu en beach handball, avec ses deux sélections engagées en demi-finales, et en taekwondo par équipes mixtes, où les Lionceaux affronteront la Jordanie en quarts de finale. À Saly, les équipes nationales masculine et féminine de beach handball tenteront de décrocher leur qualification en finale. Toujours en course dans les deux tableaux, les sélections sénégalaises auront l’occasion de se rapprocher davantage du podium et d'offrir de nouvelles médailles au pays. En taekwondo, le Sénégal disputera également un rendez-vous important. La paire nationale affrontera la Jordanie à 11 heures, au Complexe Iba-Mar-Diop, en quart de finale de l'épreuve par équipes mixtes. Cette compétition intervient après les belles performances individuelles de Marie Sarr, sacrée championne olympique des moins de 55 kg, et d’Aïda Touré, médaillée de bronze dans la catégorie des moins de 63 kg. La finale est programmée à 16h45. Autre Sénégalais attendu sur les sites de compétition, Ousmane Thioune prendra part aux dernières courses masculines de planche à voile à Saly. La 15e course est prévue à 12h47, dans une épreuve qui connaîtra son dénouement au terme de cette journée. En escrime, Tening Diallo sera également en lice au sabre individuel féminin. La Sénégalaise débutera les phases de poules à 10h30 au Centre des expositions de Diamniadio, avec une confrontation face à la Française Nina Zacchia. Cette avant-dernière journée sera aussi marquée par les débuts du breaking, nouvelle discipline au programme des JOJ, tandis que la boxe distribuera dix titres. Les compétitions prendront fin vendredi avec la cérémonie de clôture de cette première édition africaine des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse.

items.title: Tourisme au Mali: Le pari du marché intérieur
items.description: © Internet Le Salon international du tourisme de Bamako revient du 12 au 14 novembre, après quinze ans d’interruption. Guides et hôteliers attendent une relance qui transformera les visites locales en revenus réguliers. Malick Sidibé exerce le métier de guide touristique depuis une trentaine d’années. Il l’a choisi « par amour », mais les sollicitations sont devenues ponctuelles. Il accompagne notamment des excursions scolaires vers des localités proches de Bamako, comme Siby. Entre deux missions, les activités champêtres lui permettent de subvenir à ses besoins. Son parcours raconte les difficultés d’une profession dont les circuits habituels ont été bouleversés. Le retour du Salon international du tourisme de Bamako (SITOUR), annoncé au Parc national du Mali, remet ces métiers au centre des discussions. Cette cinquième édition succède à celle de 2011 et consacre ses échanges aux mutations du tourisme africain. Pour les professionnels, la promotion de la destination Mali appelle une réponse économique : comment faire des résidents une clientèle régulière, capable de soutenir les guides, les agences, les restaurants et les établissements d’hébergement ? Acteurs désœuvrés « Les activités sont au ralenti, surtout dans les zones touristiques classiques, à cause de l’insécurité », déclare Malick Sidibé. Le tourisme domestique représente pour lui une possibilité de reprendre ses activités tout en faisant découvrir aux Maliens des sites encore méconnus. La crise ouverte en 2012 a entraîné des fermetures d’établissements, des licenciements et des mises en chômage technique, rappelle Mali Tourisme. Ses conséquences touchent aussi les métiers liés aux circuits de découverte. Des témoignages des visiteurs qu’il accompagnait, le guide retient l’importance du patrimoine culturel malien. Il évoque « un trésor naturel » à structurer et à développer. Son plaidoyer s’inscrit dans une période où les autorités mettent l’accent sur la découverte du pays par ses habitants. Les statistiques récentes permettent de préciser le marché. Dans son rapport sur la balance des paiements publié en septembre 2026, la BCEAO comptabilise 164 314 visiteurs internationaux en 2024 et 103,1 milliards de francs CFA de recettes au poste « voyages ». Elle précise que ces voyageurs sont, pour une grande part, des Maliens résidant à l’étranger et des professionnels en mission. Le développement du tourisme intérieur vise une autre demande : celle des habitants qui peuvent consacrer une journée, un week-end ou un séjour à la visite du patrimoine. Initiatives de relance Bamako City Tour constitue l’une des réponses engagées. Sa quatrième édition s’est déroulée du 18 juillet au 27 septembre 2026. Le programme associe les agences de voyages, les guides et les gestionnaires de sites pour proposer des parcours de proximité. « Plusieurs enfants sont émerveillés en découvrant l’intérieur du monument de la Tour de l’Afrique », raconte Malick Sidibé. Ils passent pourtant régulièrement près de cet édifice. « Nous ne connaissons pas notre ville, à plus forte raison, notre pays », ajoute-t-il. Le bilan revendiqué par les organisateurs pour les trois premières éditions fait état d’environ 40 000 bénéficiaires de visites subventionnées à Bamako, Ségou, Sikasso, Mopti et Kayes. Une vingtaine de sites auraient été valorisés, avec la mobilisation annuelle de plus de quinze agences et d’une vingtaine de guides. Les organisateurs avancent également une portée numérique de près de 15 millions de personnes pour les contenus consacrés aux sites. Cette audience annoncée renseigne sur la visibilité du programme et se distingue de la fréquentation physique des lieux. En 2026, les formules affichées par Mali Tourisme coûtaient 2 000 francs CFA pour le parcours classique et 5 000 francs CFA pour le parcours découverte. La tarification fait partie des moyens retenus pour élargir le public des visites. L’édition 2026 a toutefois été recentrée sur Bamako, les circuits régionaux ayant été reportés pour des raisons budgétaires, selon les explications données lors de la présentation du programme en juillet. Les moyens disponibles pèsent aussi sur l’étendue des parcours proposés. Le programme 2026 annonçait des sorties chaque week-end, de 9 heures à 17 heures. Des rendez-vous réguliers et connus à l’avance peuvent aider les familles à organiser leurs loisirs et les agences à prévoir leurs équipes et leurs véhicules. La présentation claire des tarifs, des horaires et des prestations incluses facilitera la réservation et la comparaison des offres proposées aux résidents en fonction de leur budget disponible. Les créateurs de contenus participent à cette promotion. Sidy Keïta, Directeur général de Mali Tourisme, explique vouloir permettre aux Maliens de raconter eux-mêmes leur pays. Cette communication cherche à rendre les sites et les circuits plus familiers au public local. Le renouvellement des parcours compte également. Visites de monuments, promenades sur le fleuve, découverte d’espaces naturels ou du Parc des Sofas offrent différentes manières d’aborder le patrimoine. Koulikoro figure également parmi les localités retenues dans le programme « Les Maliens visitent le Mali ». Le Mois du tourisme, organisé en septembre, a également misé sur cette clientèle intérieure. Le bilan présenté à sa clôture fait état de 20 sorties et d’environ 2 000 participants, ainsi que de conférences et d’expositions. Cette première édition visait à rapprocher les habitants des richesses de leur territoire. Lors de son lancement, le ministre Mamou Daffé avait résumé la démarche par une formule : « visiter le Mali, c’est consommer malien ». L’élargissement des circuits mobilise aussi des besoins d’entretien des sites, de signalisation, de routes praticables et d’accueil. La découverte d’un lieu suppose de pouvoir y accéder et d’y trouver des conditions de visite adaptées. Le Mali compte quatre biens inscrits au Patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO : Tombouctou, les villes anciennes de Djenné, le Tombeau des Askia et les falaises de Bandiagara. La période 2026-2027, consacrée à l’éducation et à la culture, fournit aussi un cadre aux sorties scolaires et à la transmission de ce patrimoine. Soutenir les acteurs « On peut noter un ralentissement profond, sinon un arrêt, dans plusieurs activités », résume Yamadou Diallo, Secrétaire général de la Fédération des hôteliers du Mali. Les crises institutionnelle, sécuritaire et sanitaire ont durablement affecté les hébergeurs et les restaurateurs. Il accueille favorablement les opérations de promotion, tout en jugeant les ressources allouées insuffisantes. Pour lui, la relance du tourisme interne passera par un soutien aux professionnels dont les activités ont été entravées et par des moyens adaptés aux besoins de l’artisanat, de la culture et du tourisme. Le prix constitue l’une de ses préoccupations. Il préconise des subventions aux établissements et une réduction des coûts de transport pour faciliter les déplacements. Selon lui, les charges obligatoires limitent les possibilités de baisse et contribuent à des tarifs dissuasifs pour une partie des Maliens. La question concerne toute la chaîne du voyage : trajet, accès au site, restauration et, éventuellement, nuitée. Les offres destinées aux résidents ont à composer avec cette diversité de budgets et de pratiques. Une journée de visite dans sa propre ville profite différemment aux prestataires qu’un déplacement comprenant une nuitée. La semaine du SITOUR coïncide aussi avec le BAMEX, le Salon de la défense et de la sécurité, organisé du 9 au 13 novembre à Bamako. Cette clientèle de salons professionnels constitue un autre marché pour les hébergeurs. Au SITOUR, les organisateurs annoncent la gratuité des stands pour les régions et les professionnels du tourisme. Cette facilité favorise leur participation à la vitrine commerciale. Les demandes exprimées par les acteurs portent aussi sur les conditions d’exercice de leur activité tout au long de l’année. Yamadou Diallo souhaite également élargir les perspectives du salon aux États de l’AES, puis aux autres pays de la sous-région. Il y voit une possibilité de mieux promouvoir la destination Mali et de développer des échanges entre professionnels. Le retour du salon remet ces attentes à l’agenda. Pour les guides et les hébergeurs, les réservations, les prestations vendues et les séjours constituent les résultats concrets recherchés. Entre deux excursions scolaires, Malick Sidibé continue, lui, de travailler au champ. Fatoumata MAGUIRAGA

items.title: No new taxes in 2027 Budget – Ampem Nyarko
items.description: Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Ampem Nyarko has hinted that no new taxes will be introduced in the 2027 Budget. Mr. Nyarko gave the indication ahead of the presentation of the New Economy Budget on Thursday, November 12, 2026. According to him, the government does not intend to impose any new taxes on Ghanaians in the 2027 fiscal year. Ahead of the budget presentation, the Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry, for instance, warned that it would oppose any fresh tax impositions on businesses. The Chamber wants the government to instead expand the tax net and strengthen compliance to help achieve its revenue targets. Currently, the effective VAT rate is 20%, the highest personal income tax rate is 35%, while the general corporate income tax rate is 25%. The Budget presentation on Thursday is expected to provide greater clarity on the government’s revenue targets and how it intends to achieve them without introducing new taxes or increasing existing tax rates.

items.title: Impacts de la débâcle de Trump sur la politique étrangère américaine
items.description: La défaite des Républicains au Congrès pourrait redessiner le paysage du Moyen-Orient et ouvrir la voie à la montée en puissance de la Chine et de la Russie. Les problèmes internes des États-Unis comme l’inflation et l’érosion du pouvoir d’achat, qui ont lourdement pénalisé Donald Trump aux élections de mi-mandat, vont être des priorités surtout que les primaires démocrates et républicaines en vue des présidentielles de 2028 approchent. L’Amérique se tournera vers ses propres enjeux et les prochaines échéances décisives, une véritable aubaine pour la Chine et la Russie mais une source d’inquiétude pour les partenaires des États-Unis qui pourront être encore plus délaissés par l’Oncle Sam. Imed Bahri «La raison de notre défaite, c’est la guerre» . Tel fut le constat de J.D. Vance, quelques heures seulement après la déroute des Républicains aux élections de mi-mandat. Le Financial Times rappelle que le vice-président avait déjà clairement indiqué, lors de conversations privées, qu’il s’était opposé à l’attaque américano-israélienne contre l’Iran le 28 février dernier mais en déclarant publiquement son opposition, il a déclenché un débat sur l’orientation future de la politique étrangère américaine, un débat dont les répercussions dépasseront largement le Moyen-Orient. L’ampleur de la défaite républicaine, conjuguée au consensus qui se dessine quant à son lien direct avec une guerre marquée par l’arrogance au Moyen-Orient, laisse présager que les résultats des élections de mi-mandat entraîneront un nouveau recul du rôle des États-Unis sur la scène internationale. Un tel changement pourrait bouleverser le rapport de forces au Moyen-Orient, inquiéter les alliés européens et créer de nouvelles opportunités pour la Chine en Asie et dans le monde. Une vague bleue déferle sur les États-Unis Assisterons-nous à un retour à l’isolationnisme ? Anders Fogh Rasmussen, ancien secrétaire général de l’Otan, a déclaré : «Je crains que tout cela n’aboutisse à une Amérique plus isolationniste» . Si lui et le camp isolationniste du Parti républicain parviennent à imposer leur vision, les États-Unis chercheront alors à minimiser leurs pertes en Iran et à négocier le meilleur accord possible pour sauver la face dans les circonstances actuelles. Trump a l’habitude d’insulter les alliés des États-Unis et a même menacé de se retirer de l’Otan, tout en utilisant la menace de droits de douane pour obtenir des engagements d’investissement massifs du Japon et de la Corée du Sud. Les alliés traditionnels des États-Unis espèrent que le nouveau Congrès saura freiner la propension de Trump à utiliser les droits de douane comme arme de prédilection dans tout différend de politique étrangère. Des sénateurs influents discutent déjà de la possibilité d’annuler les droits de douane imposés au Canada même si le président pourrait opposer son veto à une telle mesure. Des pays comme l’Allemagne, le Royaume-Uni et le Japon espèrent que le rejet de Trump par les électeurs marquera un retour à une politique étrangère américaine plus traditionnelle où les États-Unis retrouveront leur rôle de «leader du monde libre» . Cependant, ils devraient modérer leurs attentes. Si Vance parvient à accroître son influence sur la politique étrangère de l’administration Trump, la méfiance des États-Unis envers leurs alliés européens et leur hostilité envers l’Ukraine pourraient en réalité s’accentuer. Après tout, il est le vice-président qui a prononcé un discours très controversé lors de la Conférence de Munich sur la sécurité de 2025 dans lequel il a déclaré être plus préoccupé par ce qu’il a appelé l’érosion de la démocratie en Europe occidentale que par la Russie. Il est également peu probable qu’une élection axée sur le coût de la vie et la flambée des prix de l’essence, directement liés aux derniers conflits étrangers menés par les États-Unis au XXI e siècle, débouche sur une politique étrangère et de sécurité plus interventionniste. L’issue la plus probable est un regain d’intérêt pour la politique interne en l’occurrence se tourner vers la résolution des problèmes du pays. De ce fait, les partenaires des États-Unis devront assumer une plus grande responsabilité en matière de sécurité. Trump affaibli, une aubaine pour Moscou et Pékin L’une des raisons pour lesquelles certains membres de l’administration Trump hésitaient à entrer en guerre contre l’Iran, ainsi qu’à maintenir leur soutien à l’Ukraine, était leur conviction que les États-Unis devaient concentrer leurs ressources militaires sur la préparation d’une éventuelle guerre avec la Chine. Or, Trump lui-même a manifesté peu d’intérêt pour une confrontation militaire avec Pékin, préférant se concentrer sur le commerce. Il est prévu qu’il se rende en Chine ce mois-ci pour le sommet de la Coopération économique Asie-Pacifique (Apec), qui se tiendra à Shenzhen les 18 et 19 novembre courant. On s’attend généralement à ce que, durant son séjour en Chine, il tienne un sommet trilatéral avec le président chinois Xi Jinping et le président russe Vladimir Poutine. La perspective de voir trois dirigeants aussi puissants –Xi, Poutine et Trump– réunis susciterait l’inquiétude chez les alliés des États-Unis en Europe et en Asie. Trump pourrait percevoir une telle rencontre comme un rassemblement des «Trois Grands» , une expression qui évoque les sommets de Roosevelt, Staline et Churchill durant la Seconde Guerre mondiale, la Chine remplaçant aujourd’hui la Grande-Bretagne. Ces sommets restent gravés dans les mémoires en Europe de l’Est comme un partage d’influence entre les grandes puissances, au cours duquel l’URSS s’est vue octroyer une sphère d’influence au détriment de la souveraineté de ses voisins. À Kiev, on craint que Poutine ne persuade les États-Unis et la Chine de soutenir une version moderne de la conférence de Yalta de 1945, sous la forme d’un accord de paix compromettant les intérêts ukrainiens ou adoptant le point de vue russe sur le conflit. Le reflux populiste, principale leçon de l’échec des Républicains américains Le Japon, déjà engagé dans un bras de fer tendu avec la Chine, aura également des raisons de s’inquiéter des relations de Trump avec Xi Jinping. Taïwan observera avec inquiétude tout changement potentiel de la position américaine concernant les revendications de souveraineté de la Chine sur l’île autonome. Bien que Trump apprécie le faste et les cérémonies des rencontres avec des dirigeants autocratiques comme Poutine, Xi et le dirigeant nord-coréen Kim Jong-un, l’histoire récente montre que très peu de résultats durables émergent réellement de ces sommets. De plus, les dirigeants chinois et russes savent qu’ils rencontreront un président affaibli, à l’image d’une Amérique divisée. Ils savent également qu’à l’approche de l’élection présidentielle américaine de 2028, les États-Unis se préoccuperont de plus en plus de leurs affaires intérieures, tandis que les deux principaux partis se prépareront à l’ère post-Trump. Pour la Chine et la Russie, les deux dernières années de la présidence Trump pourraient s’avérer riches en opportunités pour peser davantage sur l’échiquier international. items.title: Blé tendre : l’Algérie achète plus de 700 000 tonnes, à un prix en baisse
items.description: L’Algérie achète une nouvelle quantité de blé tendre à un prix en baisse par rapport à la commande d’il y a un mois. L’Office algérien des céréales (OAIC) a clôturé son appel d’offres de 50 000 tonnes lancé lundi 9 novembre avec l’achat de plus de 700 000 tonnes de blé meunier, rapporte l’agence Reuters, en citant des négociants européens. Le 13 octobre dernier, le même office a importé 600 000 tonnes à un prix compris entre 326 et 326,50 dollars la tonne coût et fret (c&f). Le 16 septembre, l’OACI a passé une commande de 500 000 tonnes de cette céréale à 268 et 270 dollars la tonne (coût et fret). Depuis le début de l’année, le monopole public des importations de céréales a passé commande de plus de 5,3 millions de tonnes de blé tendre . Pour les prix de la nouvelle commande, ils se situeraient autour de 313 dollars la tonne, coût et fret (c&f), selon la même source. Traditionnellement, l’OAIC ne communique pas sur ses achats à l’étranger. L’Algérie importe plus de 1,3 million de tonnes de blé tendre en moins d’un mois Pour la provenance, aucune indication officielle n’est disponible, mais selon les négociants, une part significative des 700 000 tonnes de blé tendre achetés cette fois par l’Algérie provient d’Argentine, où « la nouvelle récolte débute, donnant lieu à des offres très compétitives sur les marchés d’exportation », précise Reuters. La Roumanie et la Bulgarie pourraient également figurer parmi les fournisseurs. Pour la livraison du blé importé, elle se fera du 1er au 15 janvier et du 16 au 31 janvier 2027 s’il provient d’Europe. Pour les cargaisons en provenance d’Amérique du Sud, d’Inde ou d’Australie, il faut ajouter un mois plus tôt pour l’expédition. L’Algérie fait partie des plus grands importateurs de blé tendre au monde pour deux raisons : la faiblesse de la production et la consommation élevée de pain et de farines qui sont subventionnés par l’État. Cette année, l’Algérie devrait enregistrer une production record de céréales notamment du blé dur et de l’orge. items.title: US marine guard appears to rebuke Hegseth's delegation at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
items.description: A US Army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier appeared to rebuke Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s delegation on Wednesday after laughter could be heard as they climbed the steps of the solemn site, according to a video of the incident. Hegseth, his wife and senior aides could be seen taking pictures and speaking to each other on the steps of the memorial at Arlington National Cemetery following a Veterans Day event. Immediately after the laughter, the sentinel moved toward the group and, from a distance, shouted toward them: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” Sitting at the heart of Arlington National Cemetery, the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is a sacred site and the grave of three unknown American service members, including one from World War One. It is widely known as a place for mourning and for reflection on military service, and sentinels guard the site 24 hours a day. Asked about the incident, which was first reported by CNN , chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a statement: “The secretary and the entire department have always honoured and will always honour the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe. “While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.” Hegseth, a former Army National Guard soldier who served in Iraq, prevailed this week after the House of Representatives rejected a Republican lawmaker’s effort to impeach him. At a rare Pentagon press conference on Tuesday hours before the vote, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a farce and defended his record, which includes championing the unpopular war on Iran, launching strikes on suspected drug vessels in Latin American waters and firing senior military officers. Democrats who won control of both chambers of Congress last week have promised to investigate Hegseth for his stewardship of the US military and have not ruled out another impeachment effort.

items.title: Trump to flex muscles on Asia tour after midterms losses
items.description: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage. With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck ’ period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington. The 80-year-old Republican heads to the ASEAN summit in the Philippines and APEC summit in China from a radically transformed and hostile political landscape at home after the Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Constitutionally banned from seeking a third term in the 2028 presidential race, the unpredictable billionaire could be all the more inclined to focus his energy on the international stage. “After bad midterms, this is how presidents reset,” Edgard Kagan, an expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), told a news briefing. Iran, trade, China That is especially true for Trump on his Asian tour, where he is unlikely to be pressed publicly on domestic politics. China has described the midterms as an “internal affair” and said it is “willing to continue working” with the United States after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress. But the power shift in Washington will still be on leaders’ radars, said Joshua Kurlantzick, an expert in Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations. “In private, many (Asian) leaders are relieved,” Kurlantzick wrote in an article this month. “The Iran war has been particularly challenging for the United States’ Asian partners and allies, and they hope that after the midterm results US President Donald Trump’s decision-making on the issue will become more predictable.” Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the US and Iran is unlikely. A Democratic-controlled Congress could also take a tougher stance towards China, Kurlantzick added, backtracking on the Trump administration’s “soft approach” to Beijing that has sparked unease among US allies in Asia. Leaders in the world’s largest continent are also hoping to see Democrats push back on Trump’s barrage of tariffs on trading partners, which have stung Asian economies heavily reliant on exports. Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries has urged Congress to reassert its authority over US trade policy. The Democrats will not get an easy ride in undoing Trump’s policies, though. The president enjoys broad authority over trade and holds veto power over congressional legislation — which he has vowed to use. High-profile meeting Trump relishes dramatic gestures and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Trump told reporters this week he expects to meet Xi and Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, scheduled for November 18-19. The president said “denuclearisation” and ending the war in Iran would be on the agenda. But the bigger goal for Trump may well be a single photo of himself standing with the two other leaders he views as his great power equals, said Kurt Campbell, chair of The Asia Group and a senior diplomat during the Biden administration. “I think in many respects this could be ‘the meeting is the message’,” Campbell said. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, who watched in horror as the White House appeared to pivot towards Moscow this year, has warned against a “Yalta 2.0,” referring to Western leaders dividing Europe with the Soviet Union in 1945. Victor Cha, president of geopolitics and foreign policy and Korea chair at CSIS, said the Republicans’ midterm defeat meant a high-profile meeting was all the more likely. “One that he (Trump) has personally staked a lot of time over two terms has been on North Korea,” Cha said. “There’s nobody else in the US government that makes policy on North Korea except the president, so I think that he’ll be focused on that sort of legacy issue”.

items.title: War, poverty, repression stalk Yemen's ancient capital
items.description: Beset by poverty, war and repression, the residents of Yemen’s ancient capital Sanaa, under Houthi control for over a decade, struggle to survive. The Houthi movement seized the city in 2014, forcing the government to flee south and sparking a brutal civil war in one of the world’s poorest countries. In Sanaa, said to be one of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities, residents say they long for the pre-war days and a measure of prosperity. “Before the war, salaries were paid in full on a regular basis,” Ammar, a 24-year-old university student who asked not to use his last name for security reasons, told AFP by phone. “Today, the Houthis have divided salaries into categories,” he said. “My father is a civil servant; he falls into the category that receives half a monthly salary once every three months. My mother is a teacher and receives half-a-salary each month.” The Old City, with some buildings dating back nearly a millennium, bustles with life as vendors display foodstuffs including grains and spices in large sacks, and restaurant owners grill meat over charcoal. Unesco added the Old City to its World Heritage in Danger list in 2015, after it was damaged in fighting between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition backing the government. The historic alleys between tall, decorated mud-brick buildings are crowded with passers-by filing beneath banners reading “Boycott American and Israeli goods”. But many residents struggle to afford basic necessities. Two electricity bills “We are a family of six, and my siblings are still in school. What our parents earn is not enough to cover basic needs,” Ammar said, adding that “prices have risen sharply”. He recently lost his job at a private school, which helped him pay his university tuition fees, amid layoffs. Alongside the struggle to secure basic necessities, residents of Sanaa complain of constant power cuts. Residents pay two electricity bills, one to the authorities and another to private generators that fill in the gaps during the many blackouts. “We try to ration our electricity use as much as possible. Water is also cut off in our neighbourhood, so we have to buy water from trucks at high cost,” Iman, a mother of two, told AFP by phone. “Inflation and the soaring cost of living are not matched by any change in salaries. My husband works in the private sector and has not received a raise in three years, and there are no other job opportunities.” Living conditions have worsened in recent weeks with Saudi Arabia intensifying its airstrikes on Sanaa, according to Houthi media and officials. Since a 2022 truce between the two sides collapsed in July this year, fighting has only escalated. Forty-four people were killed in the outlying village of Al-Sharia in Sanaa province on Saturday, the Saba news agency said, citing a spokesperson for the Houthi Ministry of Health. ‘Uneducated generation’ Under the weight of poverty, the education system in Yemen has largely collapsed, and many of Sanaa’s youths have dropped out of school. Bilqis Abu-Osba, a former political science lecturer at Sanaa University who now lives outside the city, said dropouts have become endemic. Her colleagues have had to find new ways to make ends meet, like selling cakes out of their houses. Meanwhile, “the battlefields have become a refuge for young people to earn a scrap of bread”. “Poverty has played a very significant role in changing Sanaa,” she said, especially in eroding the formerly salaried middle class. She said the quality of education has also declined, not least because the Houthis have modified curricula to suit “a sectarian ideology that serves their political project”. “A new uneducated generation is now growing up, which will affect Yemen both in the present and in the future.” “Sanaa used to be a city that was culturally, politically, and socially diverse, but it is now witnessing systematic exclusion to change its identity… into a Houthi ideological identity,” Abu-Osba added. “Everyone is afraid to speak, as they can be arrested or severely punished,” she said. “There is intense terror about expressing any political opinion, even a simple one, within the city, and silence has become the norm.” Above an archway in the Old City a banner flutters with the Sarkha, the Houthis’ ubiquitous slogan: “Death to America, death to Israel, curse the Jews, victory to Islam.”

items.title: Six MDs in eight years weakened TOR – Managing Director
items.description: Frequent changes at the top of the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) during the eight years of the previous administration undermined management stability and made it difficult to address the facility’s deep-rooted operational problems, the refinery’s Managing Director, Edmond Kombat, has said. He said the refinery went through six managing directors and an interim management committee under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, leaving successive management teams with limited time to implement decisions and deliver lasting improvements. Mr Kombat said the repeated changes, at a time when TOR was not refining crude oil, contributed to the uncertainty that affected the state-owned facility. In an interview on Wednesday, November 11, he argued that turning around a refinery with complex technical and financial challenges required consistent leadership and a sustained management approach. “In eight years, they had six managing directors, including an interim management committee. And an IMC of three personnel. So let’s say roughly seven MDs. You see that the turnover was very short,” he said on Channel One TV. “They were not refining, and I think they had an instability in leadership.” Mr Kombat also identified the failure to produce independently audited financial statements over several years as a major weakness in the refinery’s governance and management. He said the absence of audited accounts made it difficult to establish a clear picture of the company’s financial position and compounded the challenges facing successive management teams. “I think they didn’t really have a lot of time to make decisions. And then an audited account just piled up. It was a management account, not an independently audited account,” he said. He disclosed that the current management had worked with the Ghana Audit Service to clear the backlog, auditing the refinery’s accounts for the seven-year period. The management had also convened an annual general meeting to consider the accounts covering 2017 to 2025, he added. Beyond the management and accounting challenges, Mr Kombat said doubts about TOR’s commercial viability within the previous administration had also raised questions about the future of the refinery. He said some officials at the Ministry of Energy had reportedly considered converting the facility into a tank farm or handing it over for alternative use rather than maintaining its refining operations. “There are indications that some of the people in the government at the Energy Ministry didn’t really believe that TOR was viable. So there was this argument about either making it a tank farm or probably giving it out,” he said. Mr Kombat, however, maintained that TOR remained a valuable national asset whose capacity should not be overlooked in discussions about its future. He cited its storage capacity of one million metric tonnes, which he said was about three times that of the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company (BOST), as well as its ability to process 45,000 barrels of crude oil per stream day. “If you have a refinery like this, the refinery of TOR, the storage is one million metric tons; it’s like three times that of BOST, and you have a refinery that is 45,000 capacity,” he said. He said the task before the current management was to consolidate the refinery’s recovery and ensure that subsequent leadership teams maintained the gains rather than allowing another cycle of instability to derail its progress.

items.title: Student Loan: Parents, NANS offer tips on how to stop double dipping by beneficiaries
items.description: By Adesina Wahab Parents under the aegis of National Parent Teacher Association of Nigeria, NAPTAN, and the National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, have offered tips on how to stop the practice of students benefitting from the Student Loan Scheme and still going ahead to collect tuition fees from their parents and guardians. The practice, labelled double dipping by the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, which gives out the loans, is gradually becoming rampant and erasing the main reason the loan scheme was initiated – take the burden of tuition payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Speaking with Thursday Learning, the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of NAPTAN, Chief Deolu Ogunbanjo, opined that such a practice negates the reason for the setting up of the scheme. “The Student Loan Scheme was set up to give access to higher education to students who would otherwise drop out because of inability to pay fees. It is also to take the burden of fee payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Such happenings may not be totally eradicated. We know how rascally some young ones can be. “I think the way out is to let the parents and guardians be aware when payments are made by NELFUND to beneficiaries. Let there be a means of notifying the parents that their children have benefitted from the scheme,” he said Similarly, the National Public Relations Officer of NANS, Comrade Obidah David, also supported notification being sent to parents of beneficiaries. “If it is a text message, they can send to parents and guardians of beneficiaries. Information on contacts of parents is always provided by students when registering. That is necessary in case of any emergency. Also, names of beneficiaries can be published whether in the traditional media or social media. There is nothing bad in that. It is for transparency, “ he stated. Recall that recently, the Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, said during a press briefing that the fund had identified cases of students allegedly accessing loan support while continuing to place the burden of tuition payments on their parents. Describing the practice as unacceptable, Sawyerr said the fund was determined to end the situation and strengthen transparency in the administration of the scheme. “This comment is based on our recognition that there are so many students out there who are double-dipping. They are taking from NELFUND and still stressing their parents. We are going to put an end to that,” he said. Under the proposed arrangement, parents would be able to confirm whether their children’s school fees had been paid through NELFUND without necessarily having access to the actual amount involved. Sawyerr said the initiative was intended to address concerns among parents who continued to shoulder the financial responsibilities of their children’s education despite the availability of government-backed loans. The development comes as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to expand access to tertiary education through the student loan programme, designed to ease financial barriers and prevent eligible students from being denied higher education because of their inability to pay institutional fees upfront. Under the arrangement, NELFUND provides loans for institutional charges, while upkeep allowances are processed separately to assist beneficiaries with their living expenses. Sawyerr explained that the exercise would go beyond the fund’s routine public awareness campaigns, which primarily inform students about the availability of the loan scheme. According to him, the new engagements would focus on educating students, parents and tertiary institutions on how the payment system works and the changes introduced to improve its administration. “We can easily do a press release and say, ‘Hey, this is what we’re doing.’ But if we don’t educate the institutions, if we don’t educate the students, everybody will still be running behind,” he said. “This is not sensitisation. This is re-education of the stakeholders and the students as to the changes that we have made in their favour,” he added. The managing director said the workshops would help eliminate confusion surrounding institutional payments, upkeep allowances and the documentation required by beneficiaries. Meanwhile, NELFUND’s Executive Director, Mustapha Iyal, provided further insight into the fund’s payment architecture, explaining that the system was designed to minimise intermediaries in the transfer of institutional fees. Iyal said the fund relied on students’ application identification numbers and wallet numbers for institutional payment processing rather than their conventional bank account numbers. “To be clear, we don’t use account numbers. We use their application ID and wallet number,” he said. The post Student Loan: Parents, NANS offer tips on how to stop double dipping by beneficiaries appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 12, 2026
items.description: The Nigerian naira opened trading on Thursday, November 12, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market, maintaining the wider spread observed earlier in the week. At the official window, data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the naira entering Thursday’s session around the ₦1,350.36 to ₦1,353.50 per dollar band. Early Thursday morning international currency feeds recorded spot quotes hovering near ₦1,345.72 per dollar, while official NFEM benchmarks reflect the closing figures from the prior trading session pending the day’s official fixing. Earlier in the week, trading at the official window saw intraday fluctuations between ₦1,349.25 and ₦1,354 per dollar, with interbank turnover reaching $248.07 million across 144 deals. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira continues to trade at a significant discount to the official rate. Currency dealers across Lagos and Abuja quoted the dollar between ₦1,411 and ₦1,420 for buying, while selling rates ranged from ₦1,419 to ₦1,430 per dollar depending on transaction volume and location. This leaves an exchange rate gap of roughly ₦68 to ₦80 per dollar between the official NFEM benchmark and street-level rates. Market analysts attribute the recent softening of the local currency to heightened seasonal foreign exchange demand from importers and travelers heading into the end-of-year period, alongside foreign portfolio investment outflows and a firmer US dollar globally. Despite the recent dip—which saw the parallel market touch a 10-month low of ₦1,430 per dollar this week—Nigeria’s gross external reserves remain sturdy at approximately $54.9 billion, well above the CBN’s full-year target of $51.04 billion, offering a substantial buffer to support market liquidity through the remainder of the fourth quarter. Traders and businesses continue to monitor daily NFEM liquidity injections and CBN updates for direction as Thursday’s trading progresses. The post Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 12, 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mississippi Democrat flips US Senate seat in stunning upset after 140 years
items.description: In a historic upset, Democrat Scott Colom has won his US Senate race in traditionally conservative Mississippi, networks projected Wednesday, making him the first African American elected to the chamber from the southern state in more than 140 years. Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney, prevailed over Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in perhaps the most extraordinary seat flip of an already extraordinary US midterm election , in which Democrats crushed the Republicans to reclaim the majority in both chambers of Congress. In a prayerful and solemn speech, Colom praised Mississippi’s long tradition of Black activism and faith in progress. “Mississippi, our prayers have often changed the course of history,” Colom told the jubilant crowd of his supporters in Jackson on Wednesday night. “God didn’t want us to get it the easy way. He wanted us to get it the Mississippi way.” Colom’s win in the deep South adds sting to the stunning rebuke of President Donald Trump as voters around the country shunned his Republican Party, even in states that had not sent a Democrat to Washington in decades. The latest win, called Wednesday by US news outlets that included CNN, NBC and CBS, will give Democrats 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with 44 for Republicans and one race — in the state of Alaska — still outstanding. The midterms result was a personal humiliation for 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept through the Republican heartland, leaving him as a lame duck president for the remaining two years of his term. The Democratic flipping of Congress signals an end to Trump’s stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, probe his administration and thwart his appointments. Including Mississippi now, Democrats flipped eight Senate seats that had been held by Republicans, scoring historic breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine —several of which had not changed hands for decades. Hyde-Smith, in office since 2018, conceded the race in a video posted to X. “While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters,” the 67-year-old senator said. “I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state.” The race in ruby red Mississippi went down to the wire — a surprise for many observers who doubted the scale of the Democratic blue wave riding on mounting anger over Trump’s harsh immigration policy, the war in Iran and rising cost of living. CNN called it for Colom on Wednesday, eight days after election night, with some 99 per cent of the vote in and the Democrat ahead of Hyde-Smith by 49pc to 48.7pc, a difference of 4,585 votes. “Blue Mississippi is here,” the US Senate’s top Democrat Chuck Schumer proclaimed on X after the projections came in. “Scott Colom is the only person who could’ve gotten this done. I knew it from the moment I met him.” Colom is set to become the first Democratic senator from Mississippi in nearly 40 years. The first Black senator the United States ever elected, Hiram Revels, was from Mississippi and served during the Reconstruction era after the Civil War. In his speech Colom referenced how Revels, a minister by training, inspired other politicians to support Colom’s Senate run through his powerful oratory. “That’s an example of the power of prayer, and through our history, there are so many people that lifted this state up through the power of prayer in very dark times,” Colom said. “It’s local people that have faith that Mississippi can make progress, and it’s local people like the people out here who had faith that we could win this election,” he added.

items.title: How did 2.6 tonnes of cocaine leave Ghana? – Kennedy Osei Nyarko questions gov’t
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Akim Swedru, Kennedy Osei Nyarko, has questioned how large quantities of cocaine continue to leave Ghana undetected following the seizure of 2.6 tonnes of the illicit drug by Spanish authorities. In a Facebook post, the legislator raised concerns about possible individuals and networks behind the trafficking operations, demanding accountability over the repeated international seizures involving shipments originating from Ghana. “How did all these tonnes of cocaine get into our country in the first place? Who is behind this and who in this administration is collaborating with them?” he questioned. His comments follow the seizure of approximately 2,600 kilogrammes of cocaine concealed in a shipment of coconuts exported from Ghana to Spain. Spanish authorities reportedly intercepted the cocaine in two shipping containers that arrived in the country from Ghana after being loaded at the Tema Port on August 2, 2026. According to details released by Spanish authorities on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, the drugs were concealed beneath false bottoms fitted into wooden crates used to transport the coconuts. Investigators tracked the consignment from the Port of Valencia to a warehouse in Almería, where the cocaine was discovered. Two suspects were arrested in connection with the operation. The seizure has renewed concerns about the possible use of Ghana’s ports and legitimate export channels by international drug trafficking networks. The latest interception comes barely two months after French customs officials seized nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine concealed in a container carrying plastic waste from Ghana. The drugs were intercepted at the Port of Dunkirk in September 2026, with the consignment estimated to be worth approximately €225 million, equivalent to about US$261 million.

items.title: Facing our past and shaping our future together – British High Commissioner to Ghana Dr. Christian Rogg writes
items.description: Britain and Ghana cannot change the past, but we can face it honestly, listen carefully and strengthen a modern partnership founded on dignity and mutual respect. A few weeks ago, I sat in Ghana’s National Theatre and watched The Darkest Chapter, a moving play by Latif Abubakar. It traces a path from the horrors of the transatlantic slave trade through decolonisation and independence to modern Ghana. One line has stayed with me: “before diplomacy, before policy, before resolutions, there were human beings”. That is where any conversation about the slave trade must begin. With the millions of people torn from their homes, families and communities. With those whose labour and suffering enriched others. And with the descendants and societies that continue to live with that history today. The transatlantic slave trade was a brutal and barbaric violation. People were denied their humanity, separated from their families, treated as property and worked to their deaths. The UK Prime Minister has expressed his “sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions of people” and recognised the way this history “still shapes our world today.” Ghana has helped ensure that the world does not look away. Its leadership in shining a spotlight on the slave trade has brought renewed attention to questions that are difficult, deeply felt and important. Ghana’s perspectives have helped shape the wider Commonwealth conversation. At the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) last week, Commonwealth leaders agreed that the time had come for a meaningful, truthful and respectful conversation to forge a common future based on equity. They welcomed the UK Government’s agreement to engage in a structured, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties, addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms. The Prime Minister also met with President Mahama during CHOGM to set out these plans and welcomed the President’s support. This is an important step, and the United Kingdom enters the dialogue seriously and respectfully. Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of the process, and the Prime Minister has said that he is open to them. A dialogue of this importance must allow those most affected to help shape it. Its outcome should not be predetermined, but neither should the depth or difficulty of the conversation be underestimated. The first responsibility is to listen. One of the privileges of serving as British High Commissioner is gaining a view of the many layers of the UK’s and Ghana’s shared history. At the British Museum this summer, I saw how one object, the Asante Ewer, can tell a story spanning medieval England, trans-Saharan trade, Asante ceremonial life and the violence and pillage of the Anglo-Asante wars. Such objects do not offer simple stories. They ask us to confront complexity and understand what they mean to different communities. Other moments remind us how relationships can change. Last year at the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park, I stood with the Duke of Edinburgh before the image of Queen Elizabeth II dancing with President Kwame Nkrumah in Accra in 1961. Ghana had won its independence only four years earlier and was inspiring movements across Africa. That photograph captured our countries’ relationship being reshaped at a decisive moment. Today, the United Kingdom and Ghana meet as sovereign partners. Our relationship is rooted not only in history, but in people, education, culture, business, security and a shared interest in prosperity. That modern partnership gives us a strong foundation for difficult conversations. We should be confident enough to discuss both progress and pain, allow space for honest disagreement, and recognise that listening is part of an equal partnership. As Ghana approaches its 70th anniversary of independence, there will be many opportunities to reflect on the journey from colonial rule to the Black Star of Africa, and on Ghana’s continuing influence in the world. The United Kingdom should take part in those conversations with humility, openness and respect. We gather to remember. We also need to listen. The dialogue agreed at CHOGM will not be simple, and there will be strongly held views. But our bilateral relationship is mature enough to face difficult history honestly, to hear each other with respect and to work together towards a common future based on dignity and equity.

items.title: Industry, manufacturing must drive 2027 Budget — Awuah
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Association of Bankers, John Awuah, says lending to the private sector has increased by more than 30 per cent over the past year, but has challenged the government to use the 2027 Budget to stimulate demand for credit by supporting viable businesses and productive sectors. He said the banking industry was seeing increased lending activity, with interest rates also easing, although the availability of bankable projects remained a major concern. Mr Awuah said the challenge facing the economy was not necessarily a shortage of funds in the banking system, but whether enough viable businesses and projects existed to attract financing and generate wider economic activity. Speaking on the PM Express programme on Joy News on Wednesday, November 11, ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, he cited Bank of Ghana data showing that credit to the private sector had expanded by more than 30 per cent between the previous year and this year. “I am quite surprised to hear that there is no money in the system,” he said, pointing to the growth in lending as evidence that banks were actively supporting businesses. He said lending rates had also declined from levels above 20 per cent to about 15 per cent, with some borrowers receiving offers at rates as low as 9.5 per cent. Those developments, he said, indicated that banks were increasingly prepared to extend credit, although access to financing would also depend on the quality and viability of projects presented to them. Budget must stimulate productive activity Mr Awuah said the 2027 Budget should help direct lending towards sectors capable of expanding production, creating jobs and increasing household incomes. He identified industry and manufacturing as areas that required greater attention, arguing that investment in those sectors could have benefits beyond the businesses receiving loans. He explained that the expansion of factories and manufacturing operations would create employment, put more income into the hands of workers and stimulate demand for goods and services. Workers with regular incomes, he said, would have greater capacity to spend at markets such as Kantamanto and other trading centres, helping to improve business activity across the economy. “If the Budget is directed towards industry and manufacturing, and we get a lot more people on the factory floors, these are all people who will be consuming, who will be going to Kantamanto and the like to purchase,” he said. He suggested that such an approach could help address concerns among traders about weak customer spending by improving employment and purchasing power. The bankable projects challenge However, Mr Awuah said increased lending and lower interest rates would not automatically translate into stronger business investment if there were insufficient projects capable of meeting banks’ financing requirements. He said the government needed to address the conditions that would encourage businesses to develop viable projects and attract investment. “Do we have sufficient bankable projects for the banks to lend to? And that is the question, the multi-million-dollar question, that we want the Minister to answer for us tomorrow,” he said. His comments come as businesses and financial sector stakeholders look to the 2027 Budget for measures to strengthen the link between banking-sector liquidity, private-sector investment and economic growth. While the expansion in private-sector credit suggests increased lending activity, the ability of businesses to turn available finance into productive investment will remain important. For Mr Awuah, the task before government is to create the conditions for more investment in industry and manufacturing, so that bank lending translates into jobs, higher incomes and stronger demand across the economy.
